### Bug Description

The Google Sheets node (operation: get many, filtering by multiple lookup columns in filtersUI) intermittently returns only the first matching row, even when several rows in the sheet match the filter criteria.

The same workflow, same filter conditions, and same underlying data sometimes correctly returns all matching rows and sometimes returns only the first one. This happens without any changes to the workflow between executions.

I also observed the same "multiple items collapse into 1" behavior today in several other node types under similar conditions: Code nodes (mode: runOnceForAllItems, returning an array of multiple objects), Merge nodes (mode: combine, and separately mode: append with multiple inputs), and the Split Out node. This suggests the issue may be in how the execution engine propagates multiple items between nodes, rather than something specific to the Google Sheets node.

What I ruled out before reporting:
- Node configuration: verified correct and unchanged between successful and failed runs (no returnAll/limit parameter set incorrectly)
- Server memory/resources: restarted the Docker container, same intermittent behavior persisted
- Reverse proxy misconfiguration: found and fixed a missing N8N_PROXY_HOPS setting (was causing unrelated ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR errors in logs), but the item-collapsing behavior persisted after this fix too

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a Google Sheets node (operation: get many/getAll), using multiple filter conditions in filtersUI to match several rows in a sheet (e.g. filter by a shared "group" column that matches 10+ rows)
2. Execute the workflow manually
3. Check the output of the Google Sheets node — sometimes it returns all matching rows correctly
4. Re-run the exact same workflow again with no changes — it sometimes returns only the first matching row instead of all of them
5. The behavior is inconsistent between runs with identical inputs and configuration

### Expected behavior

Update: confirmed this bug still occurs after updating from n8n 2.34.4 to 2.39.7, so it is not fixed in the more recent version.

### Debug Info

The Google Sheets node should consistently return all rows matching the filter conditions on every execution, given the sUpdate: confirmed this bug still occurs after updating from n8n 2.34.4 to 2.39.7, so it is not fixed in the more recent version.ame unchanged data and configuration. It should not intermittently return only the first match.

### Operating System

Ubuntu Linux 24.04

items.body:
Subject: Google Business Profile OAuth credential repeatedly loses access on scheduled runs (interactive reconnect always works, background refresh does not) — workflow cv5XW71g0osKiItD

Summary: Our workflow's Google Business Profile OAuth2 credential intermittently fails with "Unauthorized / invalid authentication credentials" on scheduled cron executions, while manually reconnecting the credential in the UI always immediately fixes it. The outage recurs anywhere from a few days to several weeks later, with no changes made on our side between occurrences. This has been happening since approximately 25 June 2026 and has survived three separate remediation attempts, each independently ruling out a category of likely cause. We believe this points to a bug in how n8n Cloud refreshes Google OAuth tokens in the background for this credential type, not a misconfiguration on our end.

Environment:

n8n Cloud instance: lendly.app.n8n.cloud
n8n version: 1.123.76 (Cloud)
Workflow: "Google Reviews", ID cv5XW71g0osKiItD
Failing node: "Reply to review" (n8n-nodes-base.googleBusinessProfile, node version 1), operation: review.reply
Credential type: Google Business Profile OAuth2 API (dedicated credential type, not generic OAuth2)
OAuth redirect URL in use: https://oauth.n8n.cloud/oauth2/callback

Symptom pattern:

Scheduled/cron-triggered executions fail with HTTP 401 Unauthorized: "Request had invalid authentication credentials. Expected OAuth 2 access token, login cookie or other valid authentication credential."
Manually reconnecting the credential (interactive Google sign-in via the credential's "Sign in with Google" button) always immediately resolves it — the very next manual test succeeds 100% of the time, no exceptions across many occurrences.
The failure then recurs later, with the interval varying from a few days up to roughly five weeks, with no pattern we've been able to correlate to anything on our side.
Note: the fact that interactive reconnect always works, but the failure only ever appears on unattended/scheduled runs, strongly suggests the problem is specific to background/silent token refresh, not the OAuth grant itself.

Timeline and remediation already attempted:

2026-06-25 — First occurrence. Diagnosed and ruled out: OAuth consent screen in Testing mode (confirmed it was already Published/verified), incorrect redirect URI, wrong credential type, tunable Workspace session-length policy (not available on our Business Starter Workspace SKU). Created a brand new OAuth 2.0 Client ID in our Google Cloud project as a precaution and re-pointed all Google Business Profile nodes to the new credential.
2026-06-25 (same evening) — Scheduled runs still failed with "credential not shared with project [our project]" even though the credential and workflow were both confirmed to be owned by the same n8n project. This pointed to what looked like stale internal ownership/permission-graph metadata on n8n's backend rather than anything visible or fixable via the UI. Workaround tried: moved the workflow out to "My workflows" and back into our team project, to force a refresh of ownership records.
2026-07-02 — Recurred on a different node ("Get many reviews") with the same signature. Re-checked the credential's Sharing tab directly this time: confirmed our project is listed as Owner (not shared in from elsewhere), which rules out a sharing/permissions misconfiguration entirely.
2026-08-07 — Recurred again on "Reply to review." Did a full audit of the Google Cloud Console side: confirmed OAuth consent screen is In Production, External, Verified, well under the 100-user cap for unverified-scope apps (ruling out Testing-mode 7-day refresh token expiry and unverified-app restrictions). Confirmed via the credential's Connection tab that n8n's Client ID matches our verified, Internal-ownership OAuth client (ruling out a stale/wrong client). Found the Client Secret field showing n8n's internal blank-value placeholder rather than a real masked value; re-entered a freshly issued Client Secret from Google Cloud Console and reconnected.
2026-09-16 — Recurred again, over five weeks after the Client Secret was re-entered and confirmed correct. This rules out the blank-secret theory as the actual cause (and logically, a genuinely blank secret should also break the interactive reconnect step, which it never has — reconnect has succeeded 100% of the time across every occurrence).

What this rules out:

Testing-mode publishing status (confirmed In Production throughout)
App verification status (confirmed Verified)
Wrong or stale OAuth Client ID referenced by the credential
Incorrect or missing Client Secret (re-issued and confirmed correct; still recurred)
Credential/workflow ownership or sharing misconfiguration within n8n (confirmed correct Owner on the Sharing tab)
Google Workspace App Access Control blocking the app (checked; not configured/restricted)
User-side revocation of the OAuth grant (confirmed still listed as active/granted in the Google Account's connected-apps list throughout)

What we'd like from support:

Any visibility your team has into background token-refresh failures or errors for this credential/workflow (workflow ID cv5XW71g0osKiltD / cv5XW71g0osKiItD — we've seen it logged both ways and want to flag the possible discrepancy in our own records, worth double-checking against your system of record) around the following recurrence dates: 25 June 2026, 2 July 2026, 7 August 2026, 16 September 2026.
Whether this is a known issue with the Google Business Profile credential type specifically, or Google's OAuth token refresh handling in n8n Cloud more broadly.
Any recommended mitigation beyond what we've already tried, given we've ruled out every user-side configuration cause we can identify.

We've built a workaround on our end (auto-resetting the affected Airtable record and alerting on failure) so this is no longer causing data loss or silent failures, but the underlying credential instability itself remains unresolved and we'd like to understand the root cause.

Happy to provide execution IDs, screenshots, or grant temporary support access to the workflow if that helps investigation.

items.body:
### Bug Description

When approving an external MCP client's OAuth access request (the "Claude wants access to your n8n instance" consent screen at /oauth/consent), clicking "Allow" fails with a database error instead of completing the consent. The error is shown both as a toast notification and inline on the consent page.

Error message

SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: NOT NULL constraint failed: oauth_user_consents.scope

Also seen in the browser as: Failed to process consent (repeated in server logs).

To Reproduce

Enable MCP Access (Settings → MCP Access → Enable MCP)
From an external MCP client (in my case, Claude), initiate a connection to the n8n instance
Browser opens https://<host>/oauth/consent showing the requested permissions (list workflows, get workflow details, execute workflows)
Click "Allow"
Error appears: "Error allowing access" / SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: NOT NULL constraint failed: oauth_user_consents.scope

Expected behavior
The consent should be recorded and the OAuth flow should complete, returning the client to the calling application with a valid access token.

Environment

n8n version: 1.123.80
Database: SQLite (default, no DB_TYPE override)
Deployment: self-hosted via official Docker image (n8nio/n8n:1.123.80), behind nginx-proxy-manager reverse proxy
Reproduced consistently across multiple attempts, including after fully recreating the container from a freshly pulled image (same digest) and after a clean re-authorization attempt — not a transient/cache issue.

Additional context
This appears to happen because the OAuth consent handler doesn't populate a scope value before inserting the row into oauth_user_consents, and that column is NOT NULL. This blocks any external MCP client (e.g. Claude) from completing an OAuth-based connection to this n8n instance's MCP server entirely.
Note: this looks related to #30501, but the failure mode is different — I get a NOT NULL constraint on the scope column on the very first consent attempt (not a UNIQUE constraint on retry), and it's reproducing on an older version (1.123.80).

### To Reproduce

1. Go to Settings → MCP Access, enable "Enable MCP"
2. From an external MCP client (e.g. Claude), initiate a connection to this n8n instance for the first time
3. Browser opens the consent screen at /oauth/consent showing the requested permissions
4. Click "Allow"
5. See error: "Error allowing access" / SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: NOT NULL constraint failed: oauth_user_consents.scope

### Expected behavior

Clicking "Allow" should record the consent and complete the OAuth flow, returning a valid access token to the calling MCP client, without any database error.

items.body:
### Bug Description

The `Mistral Cloud Chat Model` sub-node kills an Agent run with `NodeOperationError: invalid_union` whenever the model emits a **citation block**.

Mistral models can return message content as an array of chunks, one variant being `{"type": "reference", "reference_ids": [...]}` — see [Citations & References](https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/citations). The API sends those ids as **strings**; the bundled `@mistralai/mistralai` 1.x requires **integers**, so Zod rejects the chunk and the stream dies mid-answer.

The deciding line is buried deep in the union tree (all other branches are noise):

```
data.choices[0].delta.content[0].reference_ids[0]   expected number, received string
```

This is **not** #19856 (Magistral `thinking` chunks, fixed by #20853 in 1.117.0). That fix is in place — `thinking` shows up as a *valid* union member in the error below. The `reference` variant is the one that fails, and it has no issue and no fix yet.

There is no way to switch it off: the node exposes only `maxTokens`, `temperature`, `maxRetries`, `topP`, `safeMode`, `randomSeed`, and the Mistral API has no citation parameter — citations are model behaviour when grounding on documents.

### Root cause: `@mistralai/mistralai` is pinned to the 1.x line

On `master` (`@n8n/nodes-langchain` 2.40.0):

- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/package.json` → `"@langchain/mistralai": "1.0.1"` and `"@mistralai/mistralai": "^1.10.0"`
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (overrides) → `'@mistralai/mistralai': ^1.10.0`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `@mistralai/mistralai@1.10.0`

[`@mistralai/mistralai@1.10.0` → `src/models/components/referencechunk.ts`](https://github.com/mistralai/client-ts/blob/v1.10.0/src/models/components/referencechunk.ts):

```ts
reference_ids: z.array(z.number().int()),
```

This is unchanged through the whole 1.x line, including the latest [`v1.15.1`](https://github.com/mistralai/client-ts/blob/v1.15.1/src/models/components/referencechunk.ts).

Upstream fixed it in [`@mistralai/mistralai@2.2.1`](https://github.com/mistralai/client-ts/blob/v2.2.1/src/models/components/referencechunk.ts):

```ts
reference_ids: z.array(smartUnion([z.string(), z.int()])),
```

And `@langchain/mistralai` ships that SDK from **1.1.0** onwards (`"@mistralai/mistralai": "2.2.1"`). n8n is on `@langchain/mistralai` 1.0.1, which depends on `@mistralai/mistralai ^1.3.1` — so **no released n8n version contains the fix, `master` included**.

### Suggested fix

Bump `@langchain/mistralai` to >= 1.1.0 **and** raise (or drop) the `@mistralai/mistralai` entries in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/package.json` — the `^1.10.0` override alone would otherwise force the tree straight back onto the broken 1.x schema.

### To Reproduce

1. AI Agent + `Mistral Cloud Chat Model`, model `mistral-medium-3.5` (also reproduced with `mistral-large-2512`), streaming enabled.
2. Inject retrieved document snippets into the user message in a way that invites the model to cite them (in our case an explicit source marker next to each snippet).
3. Ask a question whose answer enumerates content from several documents.

It is **non-deterministic**: the same prompt in the same chat session succeeds on one run and dies on the next — it depends purely on whether the model decides to emit a citation chunk. Measured on one production workflow: 4 of 11 runs on a single enumerating prompt, and 3 of 76 runs over a day of mixed prompts.

### Expected behavior

Reference/citation chunks are parsed instead of aborting the run.

### Actual behavior

The Agent node throws mid-stream:

```
NodeOperationError: [
  {
    "code": "invalid_union",
    "unionErrors": [
      {
        "issues": [
          {
            "code": "invalid_type",
            "expected": "string",
            "received": "array",
            "path": [ "data", "choices", 0, "delta", "content" ],
            "message": "Expected string, received array"
          }
        ],
        "name": "ZodError"
      },
      ...
      // the branch that matters:
      // path: [ "data", "choices", 0, "delta", "content", 0, "reference_ids", 0 ]
      // expected number, received string
    ]
  }
]
    at wrapAsNodeOperationError (.../utils/output_parsers/langchainParserError.ts:95:9)
    at wrapLangChainParserError (.../utils/output_parsers/langchainParserError.ts:117:10)
    at .../nodes/agents/Agent/agents/ToolsAgent/V3/helpers/executeBatch.ts:110:42
    at executeBatch (.../nodes/agents/Agent/agents/ToolsAgent/V3/helpers/executeBatch.ts:107:15)
    at ExecuteContext.toolsAgentExecute (.../nodes/agents/Agent/agents/ToolsAgent/V3/execute.ts:98:8)
    at ExecuteContext.execute (.../nodes/agents/Agent/V3/AgentV3.node.ts:155:10)
```

`Description: Original error: ZodError` — failing node: the Agent, failing sub-node: `Mistral Cloud Chat Model`.

### Workaround

Replace the Mistral node with the `OpenAI Chat Model` node pointed at `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` (`options.baseURL`, `responsesApiEnabled: false`). `@langchain/openai` does not Zod-validate stream chunks, so the run completes — at the price of whatever the reference chunks carried.

### Environment

- Self-hosted (Docker). The pins quoted above are read from `master`, so current releases are affected as well.
- Models: `mistral-medium-3.5`, `mistral-large-2512`
- Nodes: `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent` (v3.1) + `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChatMistralCloud` (v1)

### Bug Description

When Qdrant is served behind a reverse proxy under a subpath (for example `https://my-server.org/qdrant/`), the Qdrant Vector Store node drops that subpath at runtime. The credential test can pass because it uses the configured `qdrantUrl` as the full base URL, but `createQdrantClient()` reconstructs the runtime client from only protocol/host/port, so requests go to `/collections` instead of `/qdrant/collections`.

This is the same user-visible signature as #15321, which was closed stale without a fix. It is separate from the Qdrant Cloud SDK compatibility failure discussed in #38401 and resolved by #37758 / n8n 2.39.x.

### To Reproduce

1. Serve Qdrant behind a reverse proxy under a path prefix such as `/qdrant`.
2. Configure the n8n Qdrant credential URL as `https://my-server.org/qdrant/`.
3. Verify the credential test succeeds.
4. Use the Qdrant Vector Store node or collection search.
5. Observe that the runtime client requests `https://my-server.org/collections` instead of `https://my-server.org/qdrant/collections`.

Repository-level reproduction on current master confirms the cause: `parseQdrantUrl()` drops `URL.pathname`, while the pinned `@qdrant/js-client-rest@1.19.0` supports carrying the path via its `prefix` option.

### Expected behavior

The runtime Qdrant client's effective REST base should match the configured credential base. Root URLs should remain unchanged; subpath URLs such as `/qdrant`, paths with a trailing slash, and nested paths such as `/a/b` should preserve the prefix on every Qdrant API call.

### Debug Info

Source-level reproduction verified against n8n master `cf49003c27c19b2490cf004a8a07429a2035222a`. The defect is isolated to URL parsing/client construction in `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/vector_store/VectorStoreQdrant/Qdrant.utils.ts`; all runtime callers route through this helper. A minimal fix and regression tests are in PR #38889.

No Help > About runtime debug bundle is available for this repository-level reproduction.

### Operating System

Windows was used for the repository-level verification; the defect is platform-independent URL handling.

### n8n Version

Current master at `cf49003c27c19b2490cf004a8a07429a2035222a` (2026-09-17 verification).

### Node.js Version

Not material to this defect; reproduction is at the URL parsing/client-construction layer on current master.

### Database

Not database-dependent; the defect occurs before Qdrant HTTP requests are formed.

### Execution mode

main (the defect is in shared Qdrant client construction and is not execution-mode specific).

### Hosting

self hosted (reverse-proxy subpath deployment).

### Provenance / separation

Split out of #38401 at the explicit request of @andreev0812: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/38401#issuecomment-5655306670

The currently pinned `@qdrant/js-client-rest@1.19.0` natively supports the required behavior through `prefix`; PR #38889 carries `URL.pathname` exactly once through that SDK-native option and includes regression coverage.

items.body:
### Bug Description

In a workflow that has an **Evaluation Trigger** alongside any other trigger, the editor auto-selects the Evaluation Trigger as the one to run. The "Execute workflow" affordance lands on it, so the obvious click starts a **full evaluation run over the entire dataset** instead of a single manual execution.

That is costly rather than merely surprising. Each dataset row executes the whole workflow, so in my case one accidental pass meant ~10 screenshot-API calls and 7 image generations against paid APIs.

The cause is in `findTriggerNodeToAutoSelect` (`packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/features/execution/executions/executions.utils.ts`):

```ts
const autoSelectPriorities: Record<string, number | undefined> = {
	[FORM_TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE]: 10,
	[WEBHOOK_NODE_TYPE]: 9,
	// ..."Other apps"
	[SCHEDULE_TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE]: 7,
	[MANUAL_TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE]: 6,
	[WORKFLOW_TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE]: 5,
	[ERROR_TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE]: 4,
};
...
const aPriority = autoSelectPriorities[a.type] ?? (isCoreNode(a) ? 0 : 8);
```

The Evaluation Trigger is not in the map, so it falls through to the `isCoreNode(...) ? 0 : 8` default. `isCoreNode` checks whether the codex categories include `Core Nodes`, and `EvaluationTrigger.node.ee.json` declares:

```json
"categories": ["Utility"]
```

So it scores **8** — the value the comment reserves for third-party "Other apps" triggers — and outranks the Manual Trigger's **6** and the Chat Trigger's **0** (Chat Trigger's codex does declare `Core Nodes`).

The `8` fallback is right for the ~90 nodes-base trigger nodes that genuinely are external-service triggers. Of those that are not categorised `Core Nodes`, the Evaluation Trigger appears to be the only first-party, non-integration one, so it is the only node this misclassifies.

The existing test in the same folder shows the intent: its `getNodeType` helper marks every type except an explicit `'app trigger'` as a core node.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a **Manual Trigger** and an **Evaluation Trigger** (any dataset source).
2. Optionally add a **Chat Trigger** as well.
3. Look at which trigger the editor marks as the one that will execute.
4. The Evaluation Trigger is selected, so "Execute workflow" starts a dataset-wide evaluation run.

Expected after the fix: the Manual Trigger is selected, and the Evaluation Trigger is used only via **Run Test** in the Evaluations tab — or when it is the only trigger present.

### Expected behavior

The Evaluation Trigger should never be the auto-selected trigger when another trigger exists, because running it is a bulk, billable operation rather than an interactive test. It should still be selected when it is the only trigger, so a workflow containing just an Evaluation Trigger is unaffected.

### Debug Info

```
n8n version: 2.38.6
Node.js: v26.7.0
Database: SQLite
Execution mode: main
Hosting: self hosted (Docker image n8nio/n8n:2.38.6)
Affected package: frontend/editor-ui
Affected function: findTriggerNodeToAutoSelect (features/execution/executions/executions.utils.ts)
Related metadata: packages/nodes-base/nodes/Evaluation/EvaluationTrigger/EvaluationTrigger.node.ee.json -> "categories": ["Utility"]
```

Reproduced with a workflow holding a Chat Trigger, a Manual Trigger and an Evaluation Trigger (Google Sheets source).

### Environment

- **Operating System:** macOS 26.6.1 (arm64) host, n8n running in Docker
- **n8n Version:** 2.38.6
- **Node.js Version:** 26.7.0
- **Database:** SQLite (default)
- **Execution mode:** main (default)
- **Hosting:** self hosted

### Bug Description

n8n version: 2.31.4 (stable)
Nodes: @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain Agent (v3.1), toolWorkflow (v2.2), toolCode (v1.3), lmChatOpenAi (v1.3), memoryPostgresChat (v1.4)
Model: gpt-4.1, temperature 0.2

## Summary

An AI Agent node with 4 connected tools (3x toolWorkflow calling sub-workflows, 1x toolCode with inline JS) intermittently receives an EMPTY observation from a tool call, even though the tool's own execution completes successfully and returns the correct data. This causes the agent to either hallucinate plausible-but-fake values, or (with the right system prompt) honestly report "the tool didn't return anything" — both are bad outcomes for a production agent.

## Evidence

With `returnIntermediateSteps: true` on the Agent node, a failing tool call looks like this in `intermediateSteps`:

    "action": { "tool": "get_pricing_info", "toolInput": {...} },
    "observation": "\"\""

Literally the 2-character string `""` — not an error, not null, just an empty JSON string — while the SAME sub-workflow's own execution record (visible separately in n8n's execution log for that nested workflow) shows it computed and returned the correct object via its terminal node, e.g.:

    { "output": "{\"precio_a_mostrar_usd\":100, ...}" }

So the tool itself never fails. The corruption happens strictly in the bridge between the tool node's output and what the LangChain Agent's tool-calling loop reads as the observation.

## What we ruled out (controlled reproduction, ~25 runs across two nearly-identical workflows)

We built a minimal replica workflow (same 4 tools, same sub-workflows, same LLM/credential) alongside the real one, and isolated variables one at a time. None of these reproduced the bug in the replica, even though the SAME exact payload reliably reproduced it on the real workflow:

- Tool type (toolCode vs. simple toolWorkflow vs. complex toolWorkflow with a 25-node sub-workflow)
- Calling 1 tool vs. calling all 4 sequentially in a single turn
- Chat memory: fresh/clean session vs. reused session with prior turns
- System prompt length/content (short generic prompt vs. the full ~4000-character production prompt)
- Session key strategy: static vs. dynamic (per-user) session key on the Postgres chat memory node
- Tool `description` field length/detail (short placeholder vs. full production description with examples)
- An extra `$fromAI`-independent input field resolving to `undefined` on one of the toolWorkflow nodes

## A possible clue: latency changes the reproduction rate

As a workaround, we added an `await this.helpers.httpRequest(...)` call (logging the real result to an external endpoint) right before each tool's return statement — adding roughly 100ms-1s of extra latency to each tool call before it returns.

Before this change: the bug reproduced in ~1 out of 7 test runs.
After adding this latency: the bug reproduced in 5 out of 5 runs.

This is not proof, but it's a strong hint that this may be a **race condition** between the tool's execution finishing and the Agent's tool-calling loop reading the result — something that a few hundred extra milliseconds of latency inside the tool makes much more likely to lose.

## Question

Has anyone seen this? Is there a known issue with the Agent v3 / toolWorkflow v2.2 combination around reading tool outputs, especially under any timing/latency pressure? We're currently mitigating in production by having each tool also log its raw result externally and a downstream node cross-check `intermediateSteps` for empty observations, substituting the real value when found — but obviously we'd rather fix the root cause.

Happy to share the full workflow JSON (sanitized) or run further tests if that would help narrow this down.

### To Reproduce

1. Create an AI Agent node (LangChain) with at least one connected tool of type toolWorkflow (or toolCode) that computes a real result and returns it via its terminal node.
2. Enable `returnIntermediateSteps: true` on the Agent node.
3. Trigger the agent with a prompt that causes it to call that tool.
4. Repeat the same exact trigger multiple times (5-10+) — the bug is intermittent, not 100% reproducible on every single run in a simplified setup, though it appeared consistently on our production workflow. Adding ~100ms-1s of extra latency inside the tool (e.g. an awaited HTTP call before the tool's return statement) made it reproduce far more reliably (5/5 runs vs. ~1/7 without the added latency).
5. Inspect the `intermediateSteps` array in the agent's execution result.

### Expected behavior

The `observation` field for each tool call in `intermediateSteps` should always contain the tool's real output (e.g. `{"precio_a_mostrar_usd":100, ...}`).

Instead, it intermittently comes back as the literal empty string `""`, even though the tool's own sub-workflow execution (visible separately in n8n's execution log) shows it computed and returned the correct data via its terminal node. The corruption happens strictly in the bridge between the tool node's output and what the Agent's tool-calling loop reads as the observation.

### Summary
The official Docker image `docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.39.6` pulled on `linux/amd64` contains an empty `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/package.json` (0 bytes). The container immediately enters a restart loop with Node.js `ERR_INVALID_PACKAGE_CONFIG`.

This was discovered while upgrading a working self-hosted instance from n8n `2.38.7` to the stable security-patched `2.39.6` referenced in the bi-weekly n8n security update.

### Environment
- Self-hosted n8n via Docker Compose
- Docker Desktop + WSL Ubuntu on Windows
- Platform: `linux/amd64`
- Working version: `2.38.7`
- Problem version: `2.39.6`
- Node.js reported by problem image: `v26.7.0`
- Image/digest observed for 2.39.6: `sha256:1eb33706d9bd902cc83f302ba8d608420dfc0815e03ee4bb1c072367d2c5e259`

### Error
```text
Node.js v26.7.0
node:internal/modules/run_main:76
  const type = getNearestParentPackageJSONType(mainPath);
               ^

Error: Invalid package config /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/package.json.
    at shouldUseESMLoader (node:internal/modules/run_main:76:16)
    at Module.executeUserEntryPoint [as runMain] (node:internal/modules/run_main:147:20)
    at node:internal/main/run_main_module:33:47 {
  code: 'ERR_INVALID_PACKAGE_CONFIG'
}
```

### Reproduction / verification
After pulling 2.39.6:
```bash
docker pull docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.39.6

docker run --rm --entrypoint sh docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.39.6 -c 'ls -lh /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/package.json && wc -c /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/package.json'
```

Result:
```text
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Sep 16 06:39 /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/package.json
0 /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/package.json
```

The image was removed and pulled again, with the same digest and the same 0-byte `package.json`.

For comparison, running the identical check against the known-working `2.38.7` image gives:
```text
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 11.8K Sep 11 07:44 /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/package.json
12088 /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/package.json
```

Platform verification for 2.39.6:
```text
Architecture=amd64 OS=linux ID=sha256:1eb33706d9bd902cc83f302ba8d608420dfc0815e03ee4bb1c072367d2c5e259
```

### Impact
`2.39.6` cannot start in this environment. The instance had to be rolled back to `2.38.7`, which leaves it below the stable security-patched version recommended in the latest n8n security advisory email.

Could you please confirm whether the `linux/amd64` image for `2.39.6` / this digest was published correctly or whether a republished image / newer stable patch is expected?

### Bug Description

The `n8nio/runners` Docker image's tag doesn't reliably reflect the n8n version actually bundled inside it. Across 5 consecutive recent patch releases, the internal `task-runner-javascript` package version lags the tag by 1-2 patches:

| n8nio/runners tag | Internal task-runner-javascript version | Matches tag? |
|---|---|---|
| 2.39.6 | 2.39.4 | ❌ |
| 2.39.5 | 2.39.3 | ❌ |
| 2.39.4 | 2.39.2 | ❌ |
| 2.39.3 | 2.39.2 | ❌ |
| 2.39.2 | 2.39.2 | ✅ |

This isn't a publish-timing/propagation issue — `n8nio/runners:2.39.6` and the corresponding `n8nio/n8n:2.39.6` core image were built **12 seconds apart** (`2026-09-16T06:41:14Z` vs `2026-09-16T06:41:26Z`), clearly from the same release automation run. The runners image for `2.39.6` is genuinely fresh, but doesn't contain what its tag says. This looks like a stale Docker layer cache in the `n8nio/runners` build not getting invalidated when the version bump lands.

Your own docs state the `n8nio/runners` image version must match the `n8nio/n8n` image version exactly, This bug means that guarantee doesn't currently hold for these releases. We hit the downstream consequence of this ourselves: pairedItem/expression data silently resolving empty for sub-workflow calls once our own core and runner images drifted apart in the same way, this appears to reproduce the identical failure mode inside n8n's own official images.


### To Reproduce

1. docker pull n8nio/runners:2.39.6
2. docker run --rm --entrypoint node n8nio/runners:2.39.6 -e "console.log(require('/opt/runners/task-runner-javascript/package.json').version)"
3. Observe output: 2.39.4 (expected 2.39.6)
4. For comparison: docker pull docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.39.6 && docker run --rm --entrypoint n8n docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.39.6 -v → correctly outputs 2.39.6
5. Repeat for 2.39.5, 2.39.4, 2.39.3 to reproduce the same pattern (see table above); 2.39.2 is the first version where both agree.

### Expected behavior

n8nio/runners:X.Y.Z's internal task-runner-javascript version should always equal X.Y.Z, matching the tag, per your own documented requirement that the runners image version must match the n8n image version.

### Debug Info

Not applicable — no running n8n instance is involved. This bug is fully reproducible via docker pull/docker run against the published images directly; see reproduction steps above.

### Operating System

N/A — reproduces on any Docker host (observed from GitLab CI runners, Ubuntu-based).

### n8n Version

n8nio/n8n:2.39.2 through 2.39.6

### Node.js Version

items.body:
## Summary

On PostgreSQL, Data Table storage usage and quota enforcement are based on `pg_total_relation_size`. Deleting rows leaves dead tuples behind, so ordinary autovacuum generally makes that space reusable inside PostgreSQL without reducing the reported physical relation size.

As a result, the Data Tables page can continue showing a storage warning after users delete rows, while the banner explicitly tells them to delete data. More importantly, once the reported physical size reaches the configured limit, n8n can reject further writes even though PostgreSQL has space from deleted rows that it could reuse.

This has been observed on an n8n Cloud Enterprise Scaling setup backed by PostgreSQL.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a PostgreSQL-backed instance with a Data Table size limit.
2. Insert enough rows, including values stored in TOAST, to cross the warning threshold.
3. Delete a substantial portion of the rows without dropping the whole Data Table.
4. Allow ordinary PostgreSQL autovacuum to run.
5. Reopen `/home/datatables` and attempt further writes near the hard limit.

## Actual behavior

- The displayed usage generally does not decrease after row deletion.
- The warning continues to say `Delete data to avoid errors`, although deletion does not reliably clear it.
- Quota validation uses the same physical-size figure and can block writes despite reusable free space in the relation.
- Clearing the warning while retaining the remaining rows may require an operational table rewrite such as `VACUUM FULL` or `pg_repack`, which is not a normal user action and has locking/capacity implications.

## Expected behavior

Deleting rows should restore capacity that n8n recognizes as usable, and the displayed metric should represent the capacity relevant to the enforced quota rather than only allocated physical relation size.

The exact implementation is open, but the behavior should satisfy these outcomes:

- A user who deletes rows can make the warning actionable without support intervention or dropping the entire Data Table.
- The hard quota does not reject writes solely because of allocated pages that PostgreSQL can reuse.
- The displayed usage and enforced quota use consistent semantics.
- If physical allocation remains the intended metric, the UI explains that deletion may not reduce it and offers a supported reclamation path instead of promising that deletion will help.

## Implementation context

`packages/cli/src/modules/data-table/data-table.repository.ts` calculates PostgreSQL usage with `pg_total_relation_size(c.oid)`, including heap, indexes, TOAST, and TOAST indexes. This is appropriate for physical allocation but does not distinguish live data from reusable space left by deleted rows.

`packages/cli/src/modules/data-table/data-table-size-validator.service.ts` compares that value directly with the warning and maximum thresholds.

Please include a PostgreSQL regression test covering insertion of TOAST-backed values, row deletion, cache reset, autovacuum/reusable space, displayed usage, and subsequent quota validation.

items.body:
### Bug Description

Agent chat integrations can reuse a conversation that was explicitly abandoned with /new after the n8n process restarts.

The /new command rotates the conversation's session generation. The active generation is stored through CacheService, while the Agent conversation history itself remains persisted in the database.

With the default memory-backed cache in regular execution mode, restarting the n8n process removes the session-generation cache entry but does not remove the previously persisted Agent conversation.

After restart, the missing generation state can be interpreted as the initial generation, causing the next incoming message to resolve back to the original pre-reset thread.

This means a conversation that the user explicitly reset can become active again after an n8n restart.

Conceptually:

base session
    ↓
/new
    ↓
generation 1
    ↓
process restart / cache loss
    ↓
generation state missing
    ↓
base session becomes active again

The persistence mismatch is:

Agent conversation history
    → persistent database

active session generation
    → CacheService

The relevant logic is in:

packages/cli/src/modules/agents/integrations/agent-chat-bridge.ts

The issue also occurs in the edge case where /new is followed by a restart before another normal message is sent:

existing conversation
→ /new
→ reset acknowledged
→ no new message
→ process restart
→ next message

The next message can resolve to the pre-reset conversation even though that conversation was explicitly abandoned.

Observed with:

n8n: 2.39.4
EXECUTIONS_MODE=regular
N8N_CACHE_BACKEND=auto
persistent database
default memory-backed cache

### To Reproduce


1. Start an Agent chat conversation.
2. Send one or more messages so the initial conversation has persisted history.
3. Send:
/new
4. Send another message. This message is associated with the new session generation.
5. Restart the n8n process.
6. Send another message to the same Agent chat integration.
7. Observe that the message can resolve back to the original conversation from before /new.

A second reproduction path is:

1. Start an Agent chat conversation and create some history.
2. Send /new.
3. Do not send another normal message.
4. Restart the n8n process.
5. Send the next message.
6. Observe that the pre-reset conversation can become active again.

Repeated resets should also be tested:

base
→ /new
→ generation 1
→ /new
→ generation 2
→ restart/cache loss

The next message must not resolve to base or generation 1.

### Expected behavior

Once /new has successfully reset a conversation, a process restart or loss of volatile cache state must not make any superseded conversation current again.

For example:

base
→ /new
→ generation 1
→ restart
→ generation 1

must hold.

It must never become:

base
→ /new
→ generation 1
→ restart
→ base

The same guarantee should hold when the restart happens immediately after /new, before the first message in the new session.

Session resets should therefore remain monotonic across process restarts and cache loss.

### Debug Info

Not available — reproduced/analyzed against the n8n 2.39.4 source tree rather than a running UI instance.
The failure was confirmed from the session-resolution and persistence paths in the 2.39.4 source. I have not yet run an end-to-end reproduction against a packaged n8n instance.



### Operating System

window 10

### n8n Version

2.39.4

### Node.js Version

n/a

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted


I investigated this further and validated a repair approach against n8n 2.39.4.

I’m not planning to submit a PR, but I’m leaving the remediation details here in case they’re useful to the maintainers.

Root cause

The /new command advances the Agent Chat session generation, but that generation is held in the cache.

With the default memory-backed cache, a process restart removes that state while the previous Agent conversation remains persisted in the database.

After restart, generation resolution can therefore fall back to the initial generation and resolve the abandoned pre-/new conversation again.

Suggested repair

Persist the session-generation authority in the database rather than treating the cache as authoritative.

A safe implementation should preserve these invariants:

The durable generation for a conversation never decreases.
/new should not acknowledge the new generation until that generation has been durably committed.
Session resolution must never resolve a generation lower than the durable generation, even if the cache is empty or stale.

The cache can still be retained as an operational projection, but it should not be the source of authority for the active generation.

The implementation I tested used a durable generation repository keyed by the base thread identity, with atomic monotonic updates for both SQLite and PostgreSQL.

The important ordering is effectively:

/new
→ determine next generation
→ atomically persist durable generation
→ update/cache projection
→ acknowledge reset

and on subsequent resolution:

durable generation
+ optional cached generation
→ resolve using at least the durable generation

This prevents cache loss or stale cache state from re-authorizing an older conversation.

Validation

The repair candidate I tested against n8n 2.39.4 passed:

workspace build
TypeScript typecheck
AgentChatBridge tests: 93/93
SQLite repository tests: 3/3
PostgreSQL repository tests: 3/3
clean patch round-trip

The implementation also needs regression coverage for:

/new followed by process restart
empty cache with a persisted higher generation
stale cache containing a lower generation
repeated resets
concurrent generation updates

The exact implementation may need adjustment against the current master, but the underlying issue is that volatile cache state should not be the authority for a reset that is expected to survive process restart.

### Bug Description

When a workflow has `saveDataSuccessExecution: "none"` and an execution's last-reached node produces zero output items, the execution never transitions out of "running" status — it stays running indefinitely.

Confirmed via a controlled A/B/A test on a live workflow (self-hosted, regular execution mode, internal task runner, SQLite):
- `saveDataSuccessExecution: "none"` → **0/10 executions completed**, all stuck `running` (observed 14+ minutes, no recovery, unaffected by container restart or n8n version upgrade)
- Changed to `saveDataSuccessExecution: "all"` (all other settings/nodes unchanged) → **12/12 executions completed successfully**
- Changed back to `"none"` → hang returned immediately, **0/10 completed**
- Changed back to `"all"` → fixed again

This affects a fairly common combination: `saveDataSuccessExecution: "none"` is a documented, commonly-recommended setting for high-execution-volume workflows to reduce DB writes, and a branch ending with zero output items is completely normal for any polling-style workflow (e.g. "check for new items, process if any exist").

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow: Schedule Trigger → HTTP Request (or any node) → a node that can return 0 items depending on upstream data (a Code node returning `[]`, or a native Split Out node splitting an empty array both reproduce it)
2. Set workflow settings: `saveDataSuccessExecution = "none"`
3. Activate. Wait for/trigger a run where the final reachable node outputs 0 items (e.g. an empty array from the upstream API/poll)
4. Observe: execution status stays "running" forever in the Executions list — no error, no timeout (even with `executionTimeout` set), no recovery

### Expected behavior

Execution should complete with status "success" regardless of item count, matching the behavior already seen when `saveDataSuccessExecution` is `"all"`.

### Workaround found

Set `saveDataSuccessExecution` to `"all"` (or presumably any value other than `"none"`) — confirmed via the A/B/A test above.

### Environment

- n8n version: reproduced on both `2.32.5` and `2.39.4` (self-hosted, Docker, regular execution mode, internal JS task runner, SQLite)
- Reproduced with both a native node (Split Out) and a Code node as the zero-item-producing node — not specific to either node type
- `executionOrder` v0 and v1 both reproduce it — not specific to execution order
- Ruled out as unrelated during investigation: task runner health/restart, `saveExecutionProgress` setting, `executionTimeout` setting (confirmed not enforced in this scenario either — separate possible issue)

Happy to provide the exact workflow JSON (sanitized) or any further debug info if useful.

### Bug Description

The published `n8nio/n8n:2.39.4` image ships OS and npm packages at versions that have **already-published fixes**, so every self-hosted operator running a CVE scanner sees a red report they cannot act on themselves.

**To be explicit about what this is and isn't:** this is not a novel vulnerability in n8n's own code, so it is not a Vulnerability Disclosure Program submission. It is a supply-chain / release-pipeline report — the image needs rebuilding (and two direct dependencies bumping). Everything below is already public in the CVE database and in Alpine's advisories.

Scanned with `trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed`. **`--ignore-unfixed` matters: every CVE listed has a fix available today.**

#### CRITICAL

| CVE | Package | Installed | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-60002 | openssh | 10.3_p1-r0 | 10.3_p1-r1 |

#### HIGH — base image (rebuild fixes these)

| CVE | Package | Installed | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-59999, CVE-2026-60000 | openssh | 10.3_p1-r0 | 10.3_p1-r1 |
| CVE-2026-14456 | libcrypto3 | 3.5.7-r1 | 3.5.8-r0 |
| CVE-2026-76956, CVE-2026-76957 | libexpat | 2.8.3-r1 | 2.8.4-r0 |

#### HIGH — bundled npm dependencies (need a version bump, not a rebuild)

| CVE | Package | Installed | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-83608, -83613, -83614, -83615, -83616, -83619 | @xmldom/xmldom | 0.8.14 | 0.8.15 / 0.9.12 |
| CVE-2026-82659, GHSA-2x7j-588g-ccc2 | nodemailer | 8.0.10 | 9.0.1 / 9.1.0 |
| CVE-2026-63376, CVE-2026-77465 | toml | 3.0.0 | 4.1.2 / 4.2.0 |
| GHSA-j95f-988m-3j2f | @tiptap/core | 3.27.0 | 3.30.5 |

That is **17 distinct CVEs**, 1 critical.

### To Reproduce

```bash
docker run --rm aquasec/trivy:latest image \
  --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed \
  docker.io/n8nio/n8n:2.39.4
```

No n8n configuration is involved — the findings come from the image contents alone.

### Expected behavior

A freshly published image contains base packages and bundled dependencies with no CVEs that already have published fixes at build time.

Two things would help beyond a one-off rebuild:

1. **Rebuild published tags on a schedule**, independent of releases, so long-lived tags don't drift away from Alpine's security updates.
2. **`openssh` accounts for the only critical and 2 of the highs.** If the ssh *client* isn't needed at runtime (it may be there for git-based operations), dropping it would remove the entire critical finding.

The npm ones — `@xmldom/xmldom`, `nodemailer`, `toml`, `@tiptap/core` — need dependency bumps rather than a rebuild. `nodemailer` in particular has been outstanding for a while: it was the sole remaining finding on 2.37.1 back in August.

### Debug Info

Not applicable — this is an image-content report rather than a runtime defect. Reproduced purely by scanning the published image, independent of any deployment.

For context, the scan was run against an unmodified upstream image pulled from Docker Hub, not a locally built or customised one.

Linux (Kubernetes, Alpine-based official image — the finding is in the image, not the host)

### Node.js Version

As bundled in the official image

items.body:
## Describe the bug

`Splunk` node, `Search Job > Create`: `earliest_time` / `latest_time` / `index_earliest` / `index_latest` are passed through `toUnixEpoch()`, which is:

```js
function toUnixEpoch(timestamp) {
    return Date.parse(timestamp) / 1000;
}
```

`Date.parse` returns `NaN` for every Splunk relative time specifier (`-15m`, `-24h`, `-1d@d`, `now`, `@d`). `NaN / 1000` is `NaN`, and `NaN` is then sent to Splunk as the literal string `NaN`.

**Splunk accepts `earliest_time=NaN` with HTTP 201 and silently ignores the bound.** So the search runs over a different — much wider — time range than the user asked for, with no error anywhere.

**Measured** against Splunk 10.2.1, `search index=_internal | stats count`:

| `earliest_time` sent | events returned |
|---|---|
| `-5m` (what the user typed) | 1,462 |
| `NaN` (what the node actually sends) | 12,027 |
| omitted entirely (all time) | 12,029 |

The node returns ~8× the requested data and reports success. For alerting, metrics or any rate-based logic this is silent data corruption rather than a visible failure.

Splunk's own API accepts relative specifiers directly — no conversion is needed:

| `earliest_time` | HTTP |
|---|---|
| `-1d@d` | 201 |
| `-15m` | 201 |
| `-24h` | 201 |

## Prior report

This was reported as #10447 (Aug 2024) and closed `NOT_PLANNED` as "working as expected… we don't currently support the relative time options". Respectfully, the measurement above shows the outcome is not merely an unsupported input: an unsupported input that is silently converted to `NaN` and then silently ignored by the server produces **wrong results that look correct**. Rejecting the input with a clear error would be "not supported"; this is not that.

## To Reproduce

1. Splunk node, Resource `Search Job`, Operation `Create`.
2. Search: `search index=_internal | stats count`
3. Additional Fields: `Earliest Time` = `-5m`, `Latest Time` = `now`.
4. Execute, then fetch the job's results.
5. Compare with the same search issued directly to `/services/search/jobs` with `earliest_time=-5m`.

The node's count matches an all-time search, not a 5-minute one.

## Expected behavior

Pass relative specifiers through unchanged (Splunk parses them natively), and apply `toUnixEpoch` only to absolute timestamps — or validate and reject an unparseable value with an explicit error instead of emitting `NaN`. Under no circumstance should an unparseable time bound become a silently wider search.

## Operating System

Docker (n8nio/n8n), macOS host

## n8n Version

2.38.7

## Node.js Version

24.x (container default)

## Database

SQLite

## Execution mode

main

## Describe the bug

`splunkApiRequest` (used by `search:create`, `search:deleteJob`, and the `user`/`report` write paths) sets `json: true` on the request **and then runs the response through `parseXml()`**. Those two are mutually exclusive: `json: true` makes the HTTP helper parse the body, so `xml2js` receives an already-parsed object rather than an XML string and rejects it.

When that parse throws, the `catch` sleeps 1s and retries **the entire POST**. Each retry dispatches another real Splunk search job.

**Measured:** one `search:create` execution dispatched **6 real Splunk search jobs** (0 before, 6 after, counted on the Splunk side by a marker in the SPL), took 3.88s wall — consistent with 5 × `sleep(1000)` — and then **reported `status: success`**, having swallowed 5 parse failures.

**Source** (`n8n-nodes-base/dist/nodes/Splunk/v2/transport/index.js`):

```js
const options = {
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
    method, form: body, qs,
    uri: `${baseUrl}${endpoint}`,
    json: true,                                    // <- parses the body
    ...
};
...
do {
    try {
        const response = await this.helpers.requestWithAuthentication.call(this, 'splunkApi', options);
        result = await parseXml(response);          // <- but this needs the raw XML string
        return result;
    } catch (error) {
        if (attempts >= 5) throw error;
        await sleep(1000);
        attempts++;                                 // retries the whole POST, not just the parse
    }
} while (true);
```

What `xml2js` does with each possible body:

| body it receives | result |
|---|---|
| the XML Splunk returns by default | OK — `{response: {sid}}` |
| a JSON string | `Non-whitespace before first tag. Char: {` |
| an already-parsed object (what `json: true` yields) | `Non-whitespace before first tag. Char: [` |

This is reachable in normal use because `populate()` copies `additionalFields` into the request body with no allowlist, so a user setting `output_mode: json` (a legitimate Splunk parameter) makes Splunk answer with JSON and triggers the path.

A retry is also the wrong remedy for a parse error — the response was already received successfully at the HTTP level, so re-issuing a non-idempotent POST cannot help and only multiplies load on the Splunk cluster.

## To Reproduce

1. Splunk node, Resource `Search Job`, Operation `Create`.
2. Search: `search index=_internal | head 1 | eval marker="probe"`
3. Additional Fields: add `output_mode` = `json`.
4. Execute once.
5. On Splunk: `GET /services/search/jobs?output_mode=json&count=0` and count jobs containing `marker="probe"`.

Observed: 6 jobs from one execution.

## Expected behavior

Pick one representation and stay with it — either drop `json: true` and keep `parseXml`, or request JSON (`output_mode=json`) and drop `parseXml`. Retries should not re-issue a POST that already succeeded at the transport level; a parse failure should surface immediately rather than being retried and then reported as success.

## Operating System

Docker (n8nio/n8n), macOS host

## n8n Version

2.38.7

## Node.js Version

24.x (container default)

## Database

SQLite

## Execution mode

## Describe the bug

`Splunk` node, `Search Result > Get Many` (`search:getResult`): the operation resolves `returnAll` and `limit` from **item index 0** instead of the current item index. For any input item after the first, the parameter lookup misses and the node emits an empty body (`{json: ""}` — an empty *string*, not rows), while the same job id returns rows over plain HTTP.

**Source** (`n8n-nodes-base/dist/nodes/Splunk/v2/helpers/utils.js`):

```js
function setReturnAllOrLimit(qs) {
    qs.count = this.getNodeParameter('returnAll', 0) ? 0 : this.getNodeParameter('limit', 0);
}
```

Both calls hardcode `0`. The operation itself correctly receives and uses the loop index `i`:

```js
async function execute(i) {
    const searchJobId = this.getNodeParameter('searchJobId', i, '', { extractValue: true });
    ...
    setReturnAllOrLimit.call(this, qs);   // <- but this ignores i
```

The same helper is used by `search:getAll`, `alert:getAll`, `report:getAll` and `user:getAll`, so the defect is not limited to `getResult`.

## To Reproduce

1. Produce 2+ items, each carrying a valid Splunk search job id (for example a Code node emitting two items).
2. Splunk node, Resource `Search Result`, Operation `Get Many`, `Search Job ID` bound to the per-item id, `Return All` on.
3. Execute.

Item 1 returns rows; subsequent items return an empty string. Fetching the same job ids with `GET /services/search/jobs/{sid}/results?output_mode=json&count=0` returns rows for all of them.

## Expected behavior

`setReturnAllOrLimit` should take the item index and pass it through, e.g. `setReturnAllOrLimit.call(this, qs, i)` with `getNodeParameter('returnAll', i)`. Every per-item operation should resolve its parameters against the item being processed.

## Operating System

Docker (n8nio/n8n), macOS host

## n8n Version

2.38.7

## Node.js Version

24.x (container default)

## Database

SQLite

## Execution mode

main

## Describe the bug

`Splunk` node, `Search Job > Create` (`search:create`): the operation reads `responseData.response.sid` unconditionally. When `exec_mode` is set to `oneshot` — one of the three values the node's own schema offers — Splunk returns the **results inline with no `sid`**, so the node throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'sid')`.

This makes `exec_mode: oneshot` unusable, despite being an offered option.

**Source** (`n8n-nodes-base/dist/nodes/Splunk/v2/actions/search/create.operation.js`):

```js
const responseData = await splunkApiRequest.call(this, 'POST', endpoint, body);
const getEndpoint = `/services/search/jobs/${responseData.response.sid}`;   // <- unconditional
const returnData = await splunkApiJsonRequest.call(this, 'GET', getEndpoint);
```

There is no guard for the oneshot response shape, which is `{fields: [...], results: [...]}` — no `sid` anywhere.

Related: the same operation never waits for the job it creates. It POSTs `/services/search/jobs` and immediately GETs the job metadata, so the returned entry is typically `dispatchState: PARSING` with no results. That is arguably by design, but it means `create` alone cannot return rows, and combined with this bug there is no working single-node path to a search result.

## To Reproduce

1. Add a Splunk node, credential pointing at any Splunk instance.
2. Resource `Search Job`, Operation `Create`.
3. Search: `search index=_internal | head 3`
4. Additional Fields > `Exec Mode` = `oneshot`.
5. Execute.

## Expected behavior

Either the node handles the oneshot response shape (returning `results` directly), or `oneshot` is removed from the `exec_mode` options so the schema does not advertise a mode the implementation cannot handle.

## Operating System

Docker (n8nio/n8n), macOS host

## n8n Version

2.38.7

## Node.js Version

24.x (container default)

## Database

SQLite

## Execution mode

main (CLI `n8n execute`, and same result in the editor UI)

items.body:
## Summary

`execute_workflow` is not callable from a ChatGPT custom MCP app when the tool schema contains `workflowInputsSchema = z.union(...)` with strict object branches.

ChatGPT exposes the union as variants with a synthetic discriminator, for example:

```json
{
  "workflowId": "<workflow-id>",
  "executionMode": "manual",
  "inputs": {
    "type": "webhook",
    "webhookData": {
      "method": "POST",
      "body": {
        "probe": "neutral"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The n8n runtime then rejects the same payload before any workflow starts:

```text
inputs: Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'type'
```

## Environment

- n8n Cloud
- n8n version: 2.37.7
- transport: n8n instance MCP over HTTPS
- client: ChatGPT custom MCP app
- authentication: OAuth2
- affected tool: `execute_workflow`

No credential values, tokens, cookies, or customer data are involved in this report.

## Expected contract

Current n8n source defines `execute_workflow.inputs` using `workflowInputsSchema`, where the webhook branch is a strict object shaped as:

```ts
{
  webhookData: {
    method?,
    query?,
    body?,
    headers?
  }
}
```

`getExecuteWorkflowCallExample()` likewise documents:

```text
{ triggerNodeName: "<node name>", inputs: { webhookData: { headers?, query?, body? } } }
```

No `type` property is part of the n8n wire contract.

Relevant source files:

- `packages/cli/src/modules/mcp/tools/execute-workflow.tool.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/modules/mcp/tools/workflow-inputs.ts`

## Reproduction

1. Expose an n8n workflow with a Webhook trigger through the n8n MCP server.
2. Connect that MCP server as a ChatGPT custom app.
3. Inspect the published `execute_workflow` schema in ChatGPT.
4. For the webhook variant, ChatGPT requires a synthetic `inputs.type = "webhook"` discriminator in addition to `inputs.webhookData`.
5. Call `execute_workflow` once using that published schema.
6. The request is rejected before workflow execution with:

```text
inputs: Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'type'
```

A neutral test using an intentionally invalid downstream body confirmed that zero new n8n executions were created, so the failure occurs at schema/runtime validation before the workflow starts.

## Why this appears to be a schema-translation compatibility issue

n8n currently publishes a strict `z.union()` of three object shapes:

- `{ chatInput }`
- `{ formData }`
- `{ webhookData }`

The ChatGPT custom-app schema adapter represents this union with a synthetic discriminator (`type`), but n8n's strict branch validators reject that extra property.

This is not a workflow, Gateway, provider-auth, or OAuth failure. The MCP connection and read operations remain healthy.

## Compatibility direction

One possible n8n-side mitigation would be to avoid exporting this input as a strict union for MCP clients that synthesize discriminators. For example, use a single strict object containing optional `chatInput`, `formData`, and `webhookData`, plus an `exactly one` refinement at runtime. That would preserve the existing wire shapes while avoiding a client-generated union discriminator.

Alternatively, the client adapter could strip its synthetic discriminator before forwarding MCP arguments.

## Request

Please triage this as an MCP schema interoperability issue and advise which side should own the compatibility fix. I can provide additional sanitized schema/readback details if useful.

items.body:
### Bug Description

AI Agent V3 can reconstruct tool-call history with a node-derived tool name instead of the canonical LangChain tool name that was originally selected by the model.

On current `master` (`f7f92c7107e72f8151392b7fdf22bdf660df6892`), `createEngineRequests()` already stores the canonical tool name in `action.metadata.toolName`, but `buildSteps.resolveToolName()` does not read that field. For standalone tools it can fall back to `nodeNameToToolName(action.nodeName)` instead.

If the node display name and the registered tool name differ — for example after a node rename/paste suffix or when a Tool Workflow uses a custom tool name — the reconstructed history can therefore expose a different tool name to the model. If the model reuses that reconstructed name on the next turn, `createEngineRequests()` cannot find it in the canonical tool list and silently filters the action out. The agent can then continue with no tool observation and eventually hit max iterations.

I reproduced this deterministically on current `master` without model/network nondeterminism.

### To Reproduce

A focused source-level reproduction is enough:

1. Register a standalone tool whose canonical LangChain name is `Ingredient_Glossary_Lookup`.
2. Give its source node the display name `Ingredient Glossary Lookup1`.
3. Let `createEngineRequests()` create an engine action. The action correctly contains:
   `metadata.toolName = "Ingredient_Glossary_Lookup"`.
4. Pass that action through `buildSteps()`.
5. Current behavior reconstructs `steps[].action.tool` as `Ingredient_Glossary_Lookup1` instead of the canonical name.
6. Feed that reconstructed name into `createEngineRequests()` with only `Ingredient_Glossary_Lookup` registered.
7. The result is an empty action list because the tool lookup fails and the item is filtered out.

Fail-before proof:
- canonical-name reconstruction test: fails
- round-trip executable-action test: fails
- matching-name control: passes
- HITL precedence control: passes
- toolkit `input.tool` precedence control: passes
- silent-drop behavior control: passes

A narrow local fix — reading `action.metadata.toolName` before falling back to `nodeNameToToolName(action.nodeName)` — makes all 6 proof cases pass while preserving HITL/toolkit precedence. The existing neighboring `buildSteps` + `createEngineRequests` suites also pass: 74/74, for 80/80 total.

### Expected behavior

When reconstructing Agent V3 tool-call history, n8n should preserve the canonical LangChain tool name that `createEngineRequests()` already stores in `action.metadata.toolName`.

The node display name should only be a final fallback when no canonical tool identity is available.

### Debug Info

Source-level deterministic proof on:

- repository: `n8n-io/n8n`
- branch: `master`
- commit: `f7f92c7107e72f8151392b7fdf22bdf660df6892`
- affected area:
  - `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/agent-execution/createEngineRequests.ts`
  - `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/agent-execution/buildSteps.ts`
  - `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/agent-execution/types.ts`
- validation:
  - fail-before causal reproduction
  - 6/6 focused proof tests after the narrow fix
  - 74/74 neighboring repository tests
  - `git diff --check` clean

`RequestResponseMetadata.toolName` is already documented as the LangChain tool name preserved for reverse lookup, so the minimal fix appears to align with the existing design rather than introduce a new behavior.

Related but not duplicates:
- #37916: V1 schema-invalid tool calls; the V3 tool-name drift was only noted later in comments.
- #36883: V3 silent tool-call drops with a different reported trigger/mechanism.

If the team agrees this is a separate V3 bug and this scope is acceptable for a community contribution, I can send the narrow fix with regression coverage.

### Environment

This report uses a deterministic source-level reproduction against current `master`; it does not depend on a specific hosted deployment, database, execution mode, or external model provider.

### Bug Description

The OpenAI node reports **no token usage for any image operation**, even though the OpenAI API returns a `usage` object for them. `promptTokens` / `completionTokens` stay empty in Evaluations and in insights, so an image workflow looks like it consumed nothing.

The metadata comes from `accumulateTokenUsage()` in `n8n-workflow`. Across the whole v2 OpenAI action set, exactly one operation calls it:

```
$ grep -rl accumulateTokenUsage packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/vendors/OpenAi/v2/actions/*/*.ts
v2/actions/text/response.operation.ts
```

All three image operations drop the data, each for a different reason:

| File | Endpoint | What happens to `usage` |
|---|---|---|
| `v2/actions/image/analyze.operation.ts` | `/responses` | Casts to `ChatResponse` — **the same type the text operation uses, which already declares `usage`** — and never reports it |
| `v2/actions/image/edit.operation.ts` | `/images/edits` | Cast to `IDataObject`; the return item is built from binary metadata only (`json: {...binaryData, data: undefined}`), so `usage` is dropped inside the function and is not reachable from `$json` downstream |
| `v2/actions/image/generate.operation.ts` | `/images/generations` | Discarded at the destructure: `const { data } = await apiRequest.call(...)` |

`analyze` is the clearest case: it calls the *same* endpoint as `text/response.operation.ts` and casts to the *same* type, which already has `usage` on it.

Note this is not recoverable by the user with an expression or a Code node — `usage` never leaves the operation, so there is no workaround.

### To Reproduce

1. Add an **OpenAI** node, set *Resource* = **Image**, *Operation* = **Generate an image** (or **Edit an image** / **Analyze image** — all three behave the same).
2. Pick a `gpt-image-*` model, give it any prompt, and run the workflow.
3. Open the execution and look at the node's metadata, or run the workflow through **Evaluations** with any metric.
4. `promptTokens` and `completionTokens` are empty / zero.
5. Compare with *Resource* = **Text**, *Operation* = **Message a model** on the same instance: token counts are populated there.

The API response really does contain the numbers — `POST /v1/images/generations` returns, for `gpt-image-1`:

```json
{
  "data": [{ "b64_json": "..." }],
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 42,
    "output_tokens": 1568,
    "total_tokens": 1610,
    "input_tokens_details": { "text_tokens": 27, "image_tokens": 15 }
  }
}
```

The OpenAI SDK already models this as `OpenAIClient.Images.ImagesResponse`, so no new type is needed.

### Expected behavior

Image operations should report token usage the same way the text operation does, so that Evaluations and insights show real numbers for image workflows:

```ts
if (response.usage) {
	accumulateTokenUsage(this, response.usage.input_tokens, response.usage.output_tokens);
}
```

Guarded, because DALL·E responses and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints may omit `usage` entirely.

Out of scope in my view: `video/generate.operation.ts` polls a job (`/videos` → `/videos/{id}`), so where usage belongs across the poll cycle is a design question rather than a guard — better as a follow-up.

### Debug Info

```
n8n version: 2.38.6
Node.js: v26.7.0
Database: SQLite
Execution mode: main
Hosting: self hosted (Docker image n8nio/n8n:2.38.6)
Affected package: @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain — nodes/vendors/OpenAi
Node type: @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.openAi, typeVersion 2.3
```

Reproduced on node typeVersion 2.3 with `gpt-image-1` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`. The code path is version-independent — no image operation has ever called `accumulateTokenUsage`.

### Environment

- **Operating System:** macOS 26.6.1 (arm64) host, n8n running in Docker
- **n8n Version:** 2.38.6
- **Node.js Version:** 26.7.0
- **Database:** SQLite (default)
- **Execution mode:** main (default)
- **Hosting:** self hosted

### Bug Description

`setWorkflowExecutionMetadata` stores custom execution data and truncates
values over 512 characters. But it logs an error when a value is over
255 characters, not 512. So a value of 256–512 characters logs an error
saying it was truncated, when it was not.

```ts
if (val.length > 255) {
    Logger.error('Custom data value over 512 characters long. Truncating to 512 characters.');
}
```

There's a second problem with the same line. Truncation is not a
failure: the execution continues and the shortened value is stored.
Logging it as `error` puts it on the same level as real faults. `warn`
seems like a better fit. The editor already shows the user a warning
about this before execution runs, so the server log is a backup signal,
not the main one.

### To Reproduce

1. Add an **Execution Data** node. Save a key with a value 300 characters
   long.
2. Run the workflow.
3. Check the server log. You'll see an `error` line saying the value was
   truncated, even though it's stored in full.

This also fires on almost every run of a workflow with an **AI Agent**
node, since it auto-saves its reply as execution data by default, and
most replies are over 255 characters.

### Expected behavior

- No log below 512 characters.
- A log at or above 512 characters, at `warn` rather than `error`.

### Debug Info

Found by reading the code on current `master`, and reproduced locally.

### Environment

- **Operating System:** any (server-side logging, not OS-specific)
- **n8n Version:** current `master`
- **Node.js Version:** 24.x
- **Database:** SQLite (default)
- **Execution mode:** queue (also happens in main mode)
- **Hosting:** self hosted

---

I have a one-line threshold fix plus the level change, with regression
tests that fail on current `master` and pass with the fix. Opening a PR
against this issue now.

## Summary

In a self-hosted Docker Compose deployment using PostgreSQL, a webhook can return the expected HTML response with the intended security headers while its n8n execution remains `running` with `finished=false`. Repeated requests accumulate unfinished executions.

This reproduced on both n8n `2.37.10` and `2.38.5` in main mode (not queue mode). The workflow is private-LAN only; no customer data, credentials, tokens, or external requests were involved.

## Topologies tested

1. Separate GET-entry and POST-action workflows, each using `Webhook -> Code -> Postgres (executeQuery) -> last node response`.
2. The same separate workflows with a terminal `Respond to Webhook` node instead of last-node response.
3. One workflow with GET and POST webhook triggers connected to the same `Code -> Postgres -> terminal Respond to Webhook` path, with no node after the response node.

For every CRM request, the HTTP response contained the expected protected HTML and `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` headers. However, the corresponding execution remained `running` and `finished=false` in PostgreSQL.

A synthetic smoke uses one GET entry plus eight POST requests (unauthenticated denial, token unlock, authorized read-only views, and revoked-grant denial). All nine requests return the expected response bodies, but their executions do not reach a terminal state.

## Environment

- n8n: `2.37.10`, then retested on `2.38.5`
- Deployment: official Docker image, Docker Compose, main mode
- Database: PostgreSQL `17.11`
- Webhook node: `n8n-nodes-base.webhook` `1.1`
- Postgres node: `n8n-nodes-base.postgres` `2.7`
- Response node, where tested: `n8n-nodes-base.respondToWebhook` `1.5`

## Control observation

On the same host and n8n instance, a different private webhook using `Webhook -> Code -> Postgres -> Respond to Webhook` completed a safe invalid/unauthorized control request without creating an unfinished execution. That suggests the problem is not a general Docker, PostgreSQL, or webhook availability failure, but is triggered by the CRM workflow path.

## Expected behavior

After a response is sent successfully, each webhook execution should become terminal (`success` or an explicit terminal error) and should not accumulate as `running`.

## Actual behavior

The response is returned successfully, but each CRM webhook execution stays `running` indefinitely. To prevent execution-history accumulation, the affected workflows were deactivated after testing.

I can provide a sanitized minimal workflow/export if that would help reproduce the issue.
