items.body:
## Describe the problem/error/question

We run a large multi-country/multi-business-type Google Maps scraping pipeline in n8n (a "Step 1" orchestrator that hands off to a "Business Type Runner" sub-workflow, which processes city x search-term combos in ~200-item chunks via a self-triggering Execute Workflow loop, so a single run can process tens of thousands of combos over many hours). The workflows were built/maintained with the help of Claude Sonnet 5 (medium reasoning effort) via n8n's MCP tooling. Flagging that only for transparency, not as a caveat: the workflow logic itself is sound (chunked, resumable, checkpointed to Postgres so it can safely run for many hours), and how it was authored has no bearing on the root cause below - this is a platform-level memory-management issue in n8n itself, not a workflow design flaw. AI-assisted ("vibe coded") workflows are increasingly the norm, so we'd ask that this be evaluated on the technical merits rather than discounted for that reason.

We triggered a run via a Form Trigger, executed as a manual/test execution in the editor. It ran successfully for about 6.5 hours (dozens of chunks completed one after another, confirmed via a Postgres "processed" flag we track per combo). Then the whole thing silently died:

- The n8n Node process crashed with `FATAL ERROR: Zone Allocation failed - process out of memory` (V8 heap exhaustion), which raises `SIGABRT` (exit code 134).
- Docker (restart policy `always`) auto-restarted the `n8n` container - twice, about 2.5 minutes apart (looks like it OOM'd again almost immediately after the first restart, before stabilizing).
- Both restarts had `OOMKilled: false` at the Docker/cgroup level and nothing in `dmesg` - this was **not** the Linux OOM-killer or a host memory limit, it was Node's own V8 heap ceiling being hit inside the process.
- On restart, n8n's own startup log correctly flagged it: `Found unfinished executions: <id1>, <id2>, <id3> - This could be due to a crash of an active workflow or a restart of n8n.`

The most confusing part for us as operators: **the Executions list kept showing all three related executions as "Running" for the better part of an hour after the process had already crashed**, with a live-looking elapsed timer. We only discovered the crash by manually cross-referencing Docker container start times and container logs on the VPS - there was no in-app signal (no error banner, no changed status, nothing in the execution list) that anything had gone wrong until we went looking at the infrastructure level ourselves.

## What is the error message (if any)?

In-app (surfaced later, after we manually stopped/re-opened the stuck execution):

```
Execution stopped at this node
n8n may have run out of memory while running this execution. More context and tips on how to avoid this in the docs (https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/scaling/memory-errors/)
```
```json
{
  "errorMessage": "Execution stopped at this node",
  "errorDescription": "n8n may have run out of memory while running this execution.",
  "errorDetails": {},
  "n8nDetails": {
    "time": "9/10/2026, 11:19:39 PM",
    "n8nVersion": "2.38.5 (Self Hosted)",
    "binaryDataMode": "filesystem",
    "cause": {
      "name": "Error",
      "message": "Node crashed, possible out-of-memory issue"
    }
  }
}
```

Container log (`docker logs`) at the actual moment of the crash:

```
<--- Last few GCs --->
[7:0x7f7f5294f000]   156439 ms: Scavenge 1092.2 (1129.9) -> 1076.3 (1140.9) MB, pooled: 0.0 MB, 10.45 / 0.00 ms (average mu = 0.993, current mu = 0.996) allocation failure;
[7:0x7f7f5294f000]   156830 ms: Scavenge 1103.0 (1140.9) -> 1076.1 (1145.9) MB, pooled: 0.0 MB, 7.91 / 0.00 ms (average mu = 0.993, current mu = 0.996) allocation failure;

FATAL ERROR: Zone Allocation failed - process out of memory
----- Native stack trace -----

Last session crashed
```

`docker inspect` on the container after restart:

```
StartedAt: 2026-09-10T22:21:50.063629036Z  RestartCount: 2  OOMKilled: false  ExitCode: 0  Error:
```

`journalctl -u docker` around the crash:

```
Sep 10 22:19:11 ... dockerd[849]: msg="restarting container" exitCode=134 exitedAt="2026-09-10 22:19:10.550260435 +0000 UTC" manualRestart=false restartCount=1 restartPolicy="{always 0}"
Sep 10 22:21:50 ... dockerd[849]: msg="restarting container" exitCode=134 exitedAt="2026-09-10 22:21:49.815209364 +0000 UTC" manualRestart=false restartCount=2 restartPolicy="{always 0}"
```

## Please share your workflow/screenshots/recording

```
(Sensitive workflow with credentials/API keys - not attaching the raw JSON. Structure: Form Trigger -> orchestrator workflow -> Execute Workflow (isolated) into a "Business Type Runner" sub-workflow -> a recursive/self-calling "chunk processor" sub-workflow that pulls ~200 combos at a time from Postgres, loops city x search-term combos through an HTTP node with pagination, appends results to Google Sheets/Postgres, and re-triggers itself via Execute Workflow for the next chunk until done. Single manual execution kicked off from a Form Trigger, expected total runtime in the 10+ hour range for the full batch. Built/maintained via Claude Sonnet 5, medium reasoning effort, using n8n's MCP tooling.)
```

## Share the output returned by the last node

N/A - there is no usable "last node" output. The execution simply stops being updated; the in-app error above is the only artifact, and it only appears if you go back into the stuck execution and it happens to resolve to an error state. For the ~50 minutes between the last visible progress and the container restart, the UI showed no output and no error at all, just "Running".

## Additional observations (may be separate issues, grouping here since they're all from the same incident)

1. **Execution status is not trustworthy for long-running executions.** All three related executions (the top-level trigger execution, the sub-workflow execution, and the in-flight chunk execution) continued to show status "Running" with an incrementing elapsed-time counter in the Executions list for roughly 45-50 minutes after the underlying Node process had already fatally crashed and been restarted by Docker. There is no polling/heartbeat check that detects "the worker that owns this execution no longer exists" and flags it promptly. Users have to notice separately (e.g. via infra monitoring) that something is wrong; n8n's own UI actively looks healthy and in-progress the whole time.

2. **Memory usage appears to be effectively unbounded for a single long manual/test execution.** Based on the GC log, heap usage climbed to ~1.1-1.15 GB and kept failing to reclaim it (repeated "Scavenge ... allocation failure") until the whole process aborted. This lines up with our workflow's shape: a single manual execution that fans out into a self-perpetuating chain of sub-workflow calls over many hours. It seems like n8n retains in-memory execution/run data for the full lifetime of the top-level manual execution (consistent with `manual: true` in the debug info and the `saveManualExecutions`/in-memory execution-data behavior), so a workflow that is *designed* to run for 10+ hours (chunked, resumable, checkpointed to an external DB precisely so it CAN run that long) is fighting the platform's own memory model for long executions. This makes n8n a poor fit for legitimately long-running batch/ETL-style workflows unless you architect around it by never using a single long manual execution - which isn't well documented as a hard requirement.

3. **The two restarts (22:19:11 and 22:21:50) both hit the same OOM wall ~2.5 minutes apart**, meaning the first auto-restart did not meaningfully recover - it just replayed the same accumulation with whatever recovery/resume logic n8n runs on startup for "unfinished executions" before OOMing again. Only the third start (or whatever came after) held.

4. **On the positive side**: the "Found unfinished executions" recovery message on restart is genuinely useful and correctly identified all 3 affected execution IDs together - that's good root-cause signal, it's just not surfaced anywhere in the UI, only in the container's stdout logs.

items.body:
### Bug Description

`.extractUrlPath()` gives one path in the editor and a different path when the workflow runs.

The editor preview and the execution use different code for this function:

- In the browser there is no isolate, so the editor always evaluates through the legacy path in `packages/workflow/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts`, which reads `new URL(value).pathname`. `renderExpression()` in `packages/workflow/src/expression.ts` says so directly: *"The VM engines (isolated-vm, quickjs) are Node-only; the browser always uses the legacy path below."*
- On the server the default engine is `vm` (`ExpressionEngineConfig.engine = 'vm'`), which runs the copy in `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts`. The `URL` constructor does not exist inside the isolate, so #26689 replaced it with a hand-written parser.

The hand-written parser slices the path out of the string and returns it as it found it. `new URL().pathname` does two more things before it returns a path: it resolves `.` and `..` segments, and it percent-encodes the path. So the two disagree, and the disagreement is silent — the field shows a green preview and then a different value is written.

The percent-encoding half is the one that bites in normal use, because it hits every non-ASCII path:

| expression on `https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Käse` | editor preview | value at execution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{ $json.url.extractUrlPath() }}` | `/wiki/K%C3%A4se` | `/wiki/Käse` |

A path taken from the preview and pasted into an HTTP Request URL works; the same path produced at execution is a different string, and any comparison, cache key or signature built from it does not match.

### To Reproduce

**In a workflow**

1. Add an Edit Fields node and set `url` (string) to `https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Käse`.
2. Add a second Edit Fields node and set `path` (string) to the expression `{{ $json.url.extractUrlPath() }}`.
3. Read the preview under the field: `/wiki/K%C3%A4se`.
4. Run the workflow and read the output of the node: `/wiki/Käse`.

Nothing reports an error in either place.

**In the repository**

`packages/workflow` runs its expression tests once for each engine (`vm`, `legacy`, `quickjs`), so one test file shows the split. Adding these cases to `packages/workflow/test/ExpressionExtensions/string-extensions.test.ts` on `master` at b4fee56db3 and running `pnpm vitest run test/ExpressionExtensions/string-extensions.test.ts` gives `Tests 12 failed | 141 passed (153)` — the `legacy-engine` project passes all 51, and `vm-engine` and `quickjs-engine` each fail the same 6:

| input | `legacy-engine` (and the editor) | `vm-engine`, `quickjs-engine` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Käse` | `/wiki/K%C3%A4se` | `/wiki/Käse` |
| `https://example.com/my report.pdf` | `/my%20report.pdf` | `/my report.pdf` |
| `https://example.com/a<b>c` | `/a%3Cb%3Ec` | `/a<b>c` |
| `https://example.com/v1/../v2/users` | `/v2/users` | `/v1/../v2/users` |
| `https://example.com/a/./b` | `/a/b` | `/a/./b` |
| `https://example.com/a/b/..` | `/a/` | `/a/b/..` |

The `legacy-engine` column is `new URL(input).pathname` in every row, because that is what the legacy path calls.

### Expected behavior

`.extractUrlPath()` returns the same path on every engine, and that path is the one `new URL(value).pathname` returns — the path the editor already shows.

Inputs that agree today must keep their current result: `https://example.com/a%2fb` stays `/a%2fb` (an already-encoded path is not encoded twice), and `https://example.com/a+b;c=d` stays `/a+b;c=d` (`+`, `;`, `=`, `'`, `|`, `:` and `@` are not in the path percent-encode set).

### Debug Info

This is a code-path difference, not an instance-specific fault, so the reproduction above is against the repository rather than a packaged install:

```
n8n repo   : master @ b4fee56db3 (version 2.39.0 in package.json)
engine     : N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE default = vm (packages/@n8n/config/src/configs/expression-engine.config.ts)
introduced : #26689, which replaced `new URL(value).pathname` with an imperative parser
Node.js    : v24.17.0
harness    : packages/workflow vitest projects vm-engine / legacy-engine / quickjs-engine
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### n8n Version

2.39.0 (master, b4fee56db3)

### Node.js Version

24.17.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

---

Per the note on AI tools in CONTRIBUTING.md: an AI assistant helped run the reproduction and draft this report. Every table above comes from a command that was actually run in this repository, and I can explain the parser and the URL path rules it has to match. I have a fix ready with regression tests and will open the PR against this issue unless you would rather take it yourselves.

### Bug Description

The MCP Client Tool node ignores the `title` field that MCP servers return for each tool. The "Tools to Include" dropdown labels every option with the machine `name` (for example `list_limetypes`, `get_limetype_properties`), even when the server supplies a human-readable `title` such as "List object types".

The MCP spec defines `title` on the tool object as the display name, distinct from `name` (the identifier used in `tools/call`):

> Intended for UI and end-user contexts — optimized to be human-readable and easily understood, even by those unfamiliar with domain-specific terminology. If not provided, the name should be used for display.

https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/schema#tool

The dropdown is built in `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/mcp/shared/runtime.ts` (`loadMcpToolOptions`), which maps each tool to `{ name: tool.name, value: tool.name, description: tool.description }` and never reads `tool.title`. The local `McpTool` type in `nodes/mcp/shared/types.ts` doesn't declare `title` either, although the `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Tool` type has had it since the 2025-06-18 spec revision.

### To Reproduce

1. Connect an MCP Client Tool node to any MCP server whose `tools/list` response includes `title` on its tools. (We hit this with our own server, but any spec-compliant server that sets `title` reproduces it.)
2. Open "Tools to Include" and switch it to "Selected".
3. Open the dropdown.
4. Every option is labelled with the snake_case `name`; the `title` is not shown anywhere.

### Expected behavior

The dropdown label should be `title` when the server provides one, falling back to `name` otherwise, as the spec says. The option `value` must stay `name`, since that is what the node sends in `tools/call` and what existing workflows have stored in `includeTools` / `excludeTools`.

### Debug Info

Reproduced against the source on `master` (n8n 2.39.0, commit 4b4d670). The mapping has been the same since the node was introduced, so this isn't tied to a particular release, database, execution mode or hosting setup.

Any

Any

### Bug Description

**Environment**
- n8n 2.37.10, self-hosted (Docker / Dokploy), Community Edition
- Sandbox: `n8n-sandbox` (bundled)
- Models tested: `anthropic/claude-opus-5` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`, BYO Anthropic key
- Reproduced both with the native Anthropic provider and with a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint

**Summary**

A single trivial question to the AI Assistant costs several dollars' worth of tokens. Two compounding causes: the agent makes many full-context round trips per question, and the invariant prefix is never cached. On self-hosted BYOK there are no credit limits, so this is billed directly to the user.

---

**Measurement 1 — Opus 5, question: "what is the Merge node for?" (6 words)**

One captured call: **30,766 input tokens / 1,015 output tokens**.

The question resolved in **4 API calls, ~75,620 input tokens total**, for ~$0.41. A short session of three brief answers reached ~$2.

**Measurement 2 — Sonnet 4.5, question: "what is a Code node?" (5 words)**

Seven consecutive calls logged for that single question (list truncated, there may be more):

| # | Input | Output | Cost | Duration |
|---|-------|--------|------|----------|
| 1 | 17,668 | 80 | $0.05420 | 2,773 ms |
| 2 | 18,332 | 56 | $0.05584 | 2,519 ms |
| 3 | 18,931 | 60 | $0.05769 | 2,577 ms |
| 4 | 19,638 | 58 | $0.05978 | 1,725 ms |
| 5 | 20,280 | 54 | $0.06165 | 2,387 ms |
| 6 | 20,877 | 85 | $0.06391 | 2,306 ms |
| 7 | 21,751 | 81 | $0.06647 | 2,448 ms |

**~137,000 input tokens and ~$0.42 for one five-word question.**

Note the output column: 54 to 85 tokens per call. These are tool calls, not answers. And input grows by ~600-700 tokens per step as tool results accumulate — while the ~17,000-token prefix is resent in full every single time.

---

**Cause 1: no prompt caching**

No `cache_control` anywhere in the request. The returned `usage` object contains only `completion_tokens` / `prompt_tokens` / `total_tokens` — no `cache_creation_input_tokens`, no `cache_read_input_tokens`.

The prefix is byte-identical across all seven calls: system prompt, skills catalog, and the full JSON schemas for `workflows`, `executions`, `credentials`, `data-tables`, `nodes`, `build-workflow`, `n8n-docs`, `mcp-servers`, `verify-built-workflow`, `research`, `ask-user`, `workspace_*`, `search_tools`, `load_tool`.

Anthropic's prompt caching references the full prefix in tools → system → messages order, exactly matching this payload. Cache reads bill at ~10% of base input. On the run above that is roughly **$0.42 → $0.05**.

**Likely root cause:** the request `User-Agent` is `ai-sdk/openai/4.0.60`. n8n appears to be talking to Anthropic through the AI SDK's OpenAI provider, which has no way to express `cache_control`. Switching to the AI SDK's native Anthropic provider would make caching expressible.

**Cause 2: excessive tool round trips**

`load_tool("n8n-docs")` returns `{"status":"not_found"}` even though `n8n-docs` is declared in the `tools` array of that same request. The agent then calls `search_tools("n8n docs")`, which returns 5 unrelated tools, before falling back to `nodes(action="describe")`. That is 2 wasted full-context round trips per occurrence.

**Cause 3: `reasoning_effort` hardcoded**

Set to `"high"` with no documented way to change it. On Opus this produced 45-second waits on trivial questions.

---

**Suggested fixes, by impact**

1. Use the AI SDK's native Anthropic provider and add `cache_control` to the tools/system prefix (~90% reduction)
2. Fix `load_tool` for tools already declared in the request
3. Expose `reasoning_effort` as a setting
4. Consider whether a documentation question needs seven agent turns

**Why this matters more on self-hosted:** on Cloud this is absorbed by the credit system and invisible. On self-hosted BYOK the pricing page states no credit limits apply — the user pays every token at full input price. The docs give no cost guidance and default to `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`.

Happy to provide the full captured payload and gateway logs.

### To Reproduce

1. Self-host n8n with the instance-ai module enabled and the bundled n8n-sandbox.
2. In Settings > AI Assistant, connect an Anthropic model with your own API key.
3. Route the requests through any proxy that logs the raw payload
   (I used Cloudflare AI Gateway, but the provider's own dashboard works too).
4. Open the AI Assistant and ask a single short documentation question,
   e.g. "what is a Code node?"
5. Inspect the logged requests.

### Expected behavior

A short documentation question should cost a small number of tokens.

Specifically:
- The invariant prefix (system prompt + tool schemas) should carry cache_control
  so that repeat calls within a session bill at Anthropic's cache-read rate
  (~10% of base input) instead of full input price.
- The usage object should report cache_creation_input_tokens and
  cache_read_input_tokens.
- load_tool should succeed for a tool already declared in the request's tools array,
  rather than returning not_found and triggering fallback round trips.

Observed instead: 7 API calls, ~137,000 input tokens, $0.42, for a five-word question.

The n8n container logs this repeatedly after each run, with different runIds:

```
Failed to clean up agent run tool results {
  runId: 'run_11989ef1-e6d7-4543-bf63-6097dbaa75be',
  error: DOMException [TimeoutError]: The operation was aborted due to timeout
}
```

The sandbox API logs show the knowledge base written file by file at session start, with `mkdir` on the same path repeated ~10 times at ~5,450 ms each, followed by hundreds of `PUT /files` at 2,000-4,000 ms. All return 200/201 — slow, not failing. The host is not resource-constrained.

Hypothesis: the run never completes cleanly, so the stream is never closed and the UI waits for an end event that never arrives.

Outbound SSE from the host is fine — a direct streaming curl to api.anthropic.com returns properly chunked `content_block_delta` events.

Happy to split this into its own issue if preferred.

items.body:
### Bug description

`.github/workflows/sec-poutine-reusable.yml` (the reusable Poutine SAST scan) reports success even when the scan itself failed to produce a usable result. The "Fail on error-level findings" step decides pass/fail purely from the exit code of:

```sh
if jq -e '.runs[].results[] | select(.level == "error")' results.sarif > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "::error::Poutine found error-level security findings:"
  jq -r '.runs[].results[] | select(.level == "error") | "  - \(.ruleId): \(.message.text)"' results.sarif
  exit 1
fi
echo "No error-level findings detected"
```

`jq -e` exits non-zero in two very different situations that this script treats identically:

1. The SARIF genuinely contains zero `level == "error"` results (a real clean scan) — `jq -e` exits `1`.
2. `results.sarif` is missing, empty, or not valid JSON — `jq` fails to even parse the file and also exits non-zero (its own error, not the "no match" exit code).

Both land in the same `else` branch, so the step prints `No error-level findings detected` and the job exits `0` in every one of these cases. A Poutine run that crashed before writing a report, was killed mid-write, or produced a truncated/corrupt `results.sarif`, is indistinguishable from a genuinely clean scan — the gate is fail-open instead of fail-closed for its own tooling failure, which defeats the purpose of a required security-scan check.

I confirmed this against the current file on `main` (verified via the GitHub API right before opening this issue) — the vulnerable pattern is still present.

### Reproduction

Locally: stub `jq` in `PATH` (or otherwise force a parse failure, e.g. truncate/corrupt `results.sarif`, or delete it before the step runs) and observe the step still prints `No error-level findings detected` and exits `0`.

### Impact

CI-hardening gap, not a runtime/product vulnerability: a broken or tampered Poutine scan silently passes as "clean" instead of failing the workflow, so the SAST gate can't be relied on to actually have run when it reports success.

### Proposed fix

A fix is already written and verified: check that `results.sarif` exists and is non-empty before parsing it, and separately distinguish `jq`'s exit codes so a genuine parse failure (anything other than `jq -e`'s documented `0`/`1`) fails the step instead of falling through to the "no findings" message. No behavior change for a normal, successful Poutine run (real findings still fail the step, a real clean scan still passes).

It's on a branch on my fork, tested with a small harness that stubs `jq` to return each of its documented exit codes against the pre- and post-change script bodies (before: missing file / empty file / malformed JSON all report "No error-level findings detected" with exit 0; after: all three fail the step, the two legitimate outcomes are unchanged):

https://github.com/holistis/n8n/commit/ebaf907f120dc3977923887645b34c4b85f24983 (branch `ci-poutine-sarif-fail-closed`)

Per CONTRIBUTING.md, I'm opening this issue first rather than a bug-fix PR with no linked issue. Happy to open the PR from that branch once this is confirmed/assigned.

### Bug Description

When the Structured Output Parser node's **Auto-Fix Format** path retries invalid output and the fix model returns a LangChain `AIMessage` whose `content` is an array of typed content blocks, n8n discards the repaired text. To trigger it in a workflow, enable **Use Responses API** on the OpenAI Chat Model connected to the auto-fix parser.

`N8nOutputFixingParser` reads the retry result with `result.content.toString()`. For content-block arrays, that produces `"[object Object]"` (or a comma-separated sequence for multiple blocks) instead of the valid JSON text inside the blocks. The second parse then fails with `Model output doesn't fit required format` even though the fix model returned valid repaired JSON.

This affects both the Structured Output Parser node's **Auto-Fix Format** option and the deprecated standalone Auto-fixing Output Parser node, which use the same parser implementation.

### To Reproduce

1. Configure a Structured Output Parser with **Auto-Fix Format** enabled.
2. Connect an OpenAI Chat Model to the auto-fix parser and enable **Options -> Use Responses API**. This toggle is required for the reproduction.
3. Supply output that fails the initial parse but can be repaired into valid JSON by the fix model.
4. Observe that the auto-fix re-parse receives `"[object Object]"` rather than the repaired JSON and fails.

A deterministic source-level reproduction is to have the retry chain resolve to:

```ts
new AIMessage({
  content: [{ type: 'text', text: '{"name":"Bob","age":28}' }],
});
```

The parser currently passes `"[object Object]"` to its second parse attempt.

### Expected behavior

The auto-fixing parser should extract the textual content from the returned `AIMessage` and re-parse the repaired JSON. Plain string content and one or more typed text content blocks should all work.

### Debug Info

Source-level reproduction against n8n `2.28.0`, base revision `08fe3cd3c6a21f86d045f1e33f30dae2e2bcbdd7`. The failure is in message-content normalization and is independent of database, execution mode, and hosting mode.

Platform-independent

2.28.0

22.22

PostgreSQL

main (default)

self hosted

items.body:
### Bug Description

In a multi-main setup, a main that acquires leadership *while its own startup activation pass is still running* silently loses the schedule and poll triggers of every workflow that pass had already processed.

`ActiveWorkflowManager.addActiveWorkflows()` guards against concurrent passes with `isActivationInProgress`, and the `@OnLeaderTakeover()` handler (`addAllNonWebhookTriggerWorkflows()`) goes through that same guard. So when the takeover lands mid-pass, the `'leadershipChange'` re-activation is dropped and only logged at `debug` level:

https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/cli/src/active-workflow-manager.ts#L393-L397

Meanwhile:

- workflows the in-flight pass processed **before** the takeover were registered as a follower — `shouldAddNonWebhookTriggers()` returned `false`, so they got their webhooks and nothing else;
- workflows processed **after** it see `isLeader === true` and are registered correctly.

The workflows in the first group are never revisited. They stay `active: true` in the database and in the UI, no activation error is recorded, `GET /workflows/:id` reports them as active, and their Schedule Triggers simply never fire again.

This is what it looked like on our instance. A main pod started as a follower, began its `init` pass, and 4 seconds later found the leader key vacant and took over:

```
05:23:01.080  info   Activated workflow "..." (ID: ...)      <- "Added webhooks" only, no triggers
05:23:05.842  info   [Instance ID main-...] Leader is now this instance
05:23:05.846  debug  Skipping activation - already in progress for mode: leadershipChange
05:23:06.118  debug  Registered cron { ..., "instanceRole": "leader" }   <- first cron of the whole boot
```

131 of 390 active workflows were processed before `05:23:05.842` and lost their non-webhook triggers; the remaining 259 were fine. One workflow on a 10-minute schedule went 10h40m without a single execution before a user reported it, and re-saving each affected workflow was the only way to recover it.

Two things make this hard to notice:

1. There is no operator-visible signal. The workflow is active everywhere you would look, and the activation-errors endpoint is empty.
2. The one log line that records it is at `debug`, which is not a level you run in production.

The window scales with the number of active workflows, so a large instance is much more likely to hit this than a small one. Any event that leaves the leader key vacant while a main is booting can trigger it — a rollout, a node eviction, an OOM of the previous leader.

### To Reproduce

On a two-main queue-mode instance:

1. Activate a workflow with a Schedule Trigger.
2. Stop the current leader so the Redis leader key expires and leadership is vacant.
3. Start a main. It begins its `init` pass as a follower and takes over a few seconds later.
4. Observe that there is no `Registered cron` line for the workflows the pass processed before the takeover (`N8N_LOG_LEVEL=debug` to see them), and that their schedules never fire — while the workflows still report as active.

The more active workflows the instance has, the wider the window and the more reliable the reproduction.

### Expected behavior

A main that becomes leader should end up with the schedule and poll triggers of every active workflow registered, regardless of whether the takeover happened before, during, or after its startup activation pass.

### Debug Info

The n8n UI debug blob is not meaningful here — the diagnosis came from the main pods' logs and the database, on a running production instance. The relevant facts:

- n8n 2.36.9, self-hosted on Kubernetes, official image, unmodified.
- Queue mode, 2 `main` replicas with `N8N_MULTI_MAIN_SETUP_ENABLED=true`, separate `worker` and `webhook` deployments, Redis for leader election, PostgreSQL for the database.
- ~390 active workflows.
- `useWorkflowPublicationService` is off, so activation goes through `addActiveWorkflows()` and not the outbox path. This is confirmed by the fact that the `Skipping activation` line is reached at all — the feature-flag early-return in `addAllNonWebhookTriggerWorkflows()` sits before it.
- Node.js version is whatever the official 2.36.9 image ships; we do not override it.
- The code path is unchanged on `master` (`2.37.0`) at the time of writing, so this is not fixed in the current release.

### Operating System

Linux (official n8n Docker image on Kubernetes)

### n8n Version

2.36.9 (also present on master, 2.37.0)

### Node.js Version

As shipped in the official n8n Docker image for 2.36.9 (not overridden)

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

queue

### Hosting

self hosted

---

### Proposed fix

I have pushed a candidate fix as a draft PR: **#38008** (branch `fluty84:fix/multi-main-leader-takeover-mid-activation`). It queues the leadership change instead of dropping it and re-runs activation once the in-flight pass finishes, tears down non-webhook triggers before the re-run so the ones the interleaved pass already registered as leader are not registered twice, and raises the dropped-activation log from `debug` to `warn`. It includes three unit tests, one of which pins the ordering.

It is a draft because CI on a fork PR sits at `action_required` until a maintainer approves the workflow runs, and I could not run `packages/cli`'s unit suite locally (unrelated macOS issue with `class-validator` resolving to its TS source, which also happens on a pristine `master`). Treat it as a worked example of the fix rather than a finished patch — happy to adapt it to whatever shape you prefer, or to just leave the analysis here if you would rather fix it yourselves.

### Related

- #27416 — same code path (activation during startup and leadership change in multi-main), different failure: that one is about activation failures writing `active: false`. Still open.
- #30607 — duplicate scheduled executions, which is what this race can also produce if the re-run is added without the teardown mentioned above.

items.body:
### Bug Description

A model-generated tool call that fails the tool's Zod schema validation **terminates the entire AI Agent execution**. The end user receives nothing.

With `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent` typeVersion 1.9 (AgentV1), when the model emits a `tool_use` block whose `input` does not satisfy the tool's generated schema, the node raises:

```
NodeOperationError: Received tool input did not match expected schema
✖ Required
  → at query
```

The workflow ends with status `error`, `lastNodeExecuted: AI Agent`, and no output. A single malformed tool call from the model destroys the whole run, including all work already completed in earlier iterations of the same execution.

This is reachable through ordinary configuration and ordinary model behaviour. Anthropic tool use is non-strict by default, which means a JSON Schema `required` list guides generation but does not constrain it — the model may emit `input: {}`. We measured this directly at the provider boundary with a transparent proxy between n8n and `api.anthropic.com`: **33 of 267 `tool_use` blocks (12.4%) had a completely empty `input: {}`**, on tools that declared required parameters. So the invalid input originates with the model, not with n8n, and n8n's handling of it is what turns a recoverable event into total loss.

There is a perverse consequence: an **honest** schema is the one that breaks production. Declaring a tool parameter required makes runs fail; supplying a default to `$fromAI` makes the parameter optional in the emitted schema and the agent survives. Users are pushed toward less accurate tool schemas to keep the agent alive.

### To Reproduce

1. Build an AI Agent (typeVersion 1.9) with an Anthropic Chat Model and at least one sub-workflow tool.
2. Give the tool one parameter via `$fromAI` **with no default**, e.g. `{{ $fromAI('query', 'One focused search query', 'string') }}`. This produces a schema with `required: ["query"]`. (Supplying a 4th argument instead adds `.default(...)`, which makes the parameter optional and hides the bug.)
3. Run a workload where the model issues many tool calls — ours was 25 questions, each producing several.
4. Whenever the model emits a tool call with no arguments, the execution dies with the error above.

Measured over the same 25-question set, changing only whether the parameter carries a default:

| configuration | answers delivered | failed executions |
|---|---|---|
| parameter optional (default supplied) | 25 / 25 | 0 |
| **parameter required (no default)** | **22 / 25** | **3** |

All three failures were `Received tool input did not match expected schema`.

### Expected behavior

An invalid tool input should be returned to the model as a recoverable error observation, and the agent loop should continue, rather than terminating the execution.

Concretely: surface the validation failure as a tool result marked as an error, so the model can correct itself and retry on the next iteration. Anthropic explicitly supports continuing the conversation this way — returning a `tool_result` with `is_error: true`, after which the model can attempt a corrected call.

This matters beyond one provider. The same path is reachable from any model that emits a schema-invalid tool call, from tools whose schemas cannot use constrained generation, and from application-level validation stricter than JSON Schema.

We observed that AgentV3 appears to route failed AI-tool executions back through the execution engine as error results. If V1 is intentionally frozen and V3 is the supported path for this behaviour, **saying so in the docs would fully resolve this report** — we are not asking for a V1 backport.

Related: #37915 (same report, auto-closed as a feature request; it is a defect with data loss, so re-filing on the bug template) and #37914 (`strict: true` passthrough, which would prevent the invalid calls at source for Anthropic but does not address the fatal handling).

### Debug Info

Assembled from the deployment and the n8n API rather than Help → About, as this instance is accessed programmatically:

```
n8n:                       2.37.7 (self-hosted, official image)
agent node:                @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent  typeVersion 1.9  (AgentV1)
model node:                @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChatAnthropic  typeVersion 1.6
@langchain/anthropic:      1.5.6  (per the 2.37.7 workspace catalog)
model:                     claude-opus-5, adaptive thinking, streaming, prompt caching 5m
tools:                     4 client tools, all sub-workflow backed (toolWorkflow)
failing execution status:  error   lastNodeExecuted: AI Agent   no output produced
```

### Operating System

Linux (official n8n Docker image, hosted on Render)

### n8n Version

2.37.7

### Node.js Version

24.x (official image for the 2.37.7 tag; `engines.node >= 24.0.0`)

items.body:
## Bug Description

When several credentials use an SSH tunnel with identical SSH settings (same host, port, user and key), n8n shares one `ssh2` client between them via `SSHClientsManager`. That shared client is destroyed as soon as the **first** credential that opened it has its connection pool expire, even while other credentials are still actively using it. Those other credentials then hang on "Executing node…" and fail, and keep failing until their own pool is dropped or another credential rebuilds the client.

Root cause, from the current `master`:

- `packages/core/src/execution-engine/ssh-clients-manager.ts`, `getClient()`: clients are cached by `sha1(JSON.stringify(sshConfig))`. On a cache hit the method only does `existing.lastUsed = new Date()` and returns the client; the caller's `abortController` is **not** registered. Only the first caller's `AbortController` is stored with the registration, and its `abort` listener calls `cleanupClient(key)`, which runs `registration.client.end()`.
- `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Postgres/transport/index.ts`: every Postgres credential gets its own pool via `ConnectionPoolManager` and passes **its own** `abortController` to `this.helpers.getSSHClient(credentials, abortController)`. The local TCP proxy calls `sshClient.forwardOut(...)` on whatever client it was handed.
- `packages/nodes-base/utils/connection-pool-manager.ts`: pools have a 5 minute TTL (`5 * 60 * 1000`, cleanup every 60 s). When a pool is reaped, `registration.abortController.abort()` is called.

So: credential A's pool creates the shared client and becomes its "owner". Credential B attaches to the same client (cache hit, controller ignored). Five minutes after A's **last use**, A's pool is reaped → A's controller aborts → `cleanupClient` → `client.end()`. B's proxy still points at the ended client; its next `forwardOut` fails, B's execution hangs and then errors. B keeps failing on retries until its pool is dropped. A, or any other credential, opens a fresh client on its next run and works.

This is different from #12807 / #16054 (single-credential pool not being recreated). That fix is present in the version we run; the failure here only happens with two or more credentials sharing one SSH client.

## To Reproduce

Setup: two Postgres credentials pointing at **different** databases, both with "SSH Tunnel" enabled and **identical** SSH host, port, user and private key.

1. Run a workflow using credential A once.
2. Within a minute, start running a workflow using credential B once per minute. It works.
3. About five minutes after A's run (A's pool TTL), B hangs on "Executing node…" and then fails.
4. Run B again: fails again.
5. Run A: works (opens a new SSH connection). B works again only after its own pool has been reaped or n8n is restarted.

We confirmed the mechanism from the SSH server side (Amazon Linux 2023, OpenSSH 9.9). All times UTC, 2026-09-05. Exact times are from the SSH server's log; times marked `~` are the manual runs as triggered in the n8n UI, and for the failing runs the point is precisely that nothing reached the server:

```
 15:01:09  A runs -> new SSH login (shared client created, owned by A's pool)
~15:05:00  B runs through the same SSH connection -> works
 15:06:37  n8n sends SSH disconnect: A's pool TTL (5 min after A's last use)
           rounded up to the next 60 s cleanup tick. B had refreshed the SSH
           client's lastUsed ~90 s earlier, so this is not the SSH idle timeout.
~15:07:00  B runs -> hangs on "Executing node…"; NO connection attempt reaches the server
~15:08:30  B runs again -> fails; still no connection attempt
 15:09:08  A runs -> new SSH login -> works
```

Confirming test: after giving every credential a **different SSH port** (so the cache key differs), the server held 8 concurrent SSH sessions, one per credential, each expiring independently 5 minutes after its own last use, and no credential failed.

## Expected behavior

A shared SSH client should not be ended while other dependents are still using it. Either:

- register every caller's `AbortController` on a cache hit and only end the client when the last dependent has aborted (reference counting), or
- when the client is ended for any reason, abort **all** dependents' controllers so their proxies and pools are torn down and recreated on next use, instead of leaving them pointing at a dead client.

## Debug Info


items.body:
### Bug Description

The SSH client manager can close a replacement connection when an old client emits a delayed event. Cleanup selects the current registration by the SSH configuration hash. A replacement client uses the same hash when its connection settings match.

The manager also retains the old client-to-hash mapping after cleanup. A later usage update from that old client can update the replacement client's idle timestamp.

A synchronous exception from Client.connect() can leave a rejected connection promise in the cache. Later calls with the same settings reuse the rejection instead of attempting a new connection.

### Steps to Reproduce

Use a local unit test with mocked SSH transport. No external SSH server is required.

1. Obtain client A from SSHClientsManager.getClient().
2. Emit end on A to remove its registration.
3. Obtain client B with the same connection settings.
4. Emit close on A.
5. Observe that the manager calls end on B and removes B from its cache.

The same sequence also fails with a delayed end or error event from A.

For idle tracking, call updateLastUsed(A) after B is registered. Observe that B's idle time changes.

For connection failure, make connect() throw synchronously. Call getClient() twice with the same settings. Observe that connect() runs only once because the rejected promise remains cached.

### Expected Behavior

An event from A must only clean up A's registration. It must not close B or abort B's controller. Usage updates from a removed client must not change the replacement's idle time. A failed connection must be removed from the cache so a later call can attempt a new connection.

### Bug Description

A workflow with an IF node ("Route by Mascot") feeding two branches (one via Execute Workflow in fire-and-forget/integrated mode, one direct) into a Merge node ("Merge Mascot & Non-Mascot Branches", append mode) reliably fails to execute the Merge node. Execution reports lastNodeExecuted: "Route by Mascot", status success, no error, and the correct [2,0] item split on the IF node — but Merge never fires and nothing downstream runs. Completes in ~200-250ms (not a timeout/hang).

### To Reproduce

- Deterministic across 5 real attempts on the live 48-node workflow (execution IDs 1272, 1293, 1296, 1299) and 1 full verbatim clone (1305).
- An isolated repro using byte-for-byte identical copies of the exact IF → Execute Workflow → Merge node combination completes successfully in <30ms — it does NOT reproduce the bug.
- The bug only reproduces when the full 48-node graph is present. Bisecting the graph down to a minimal repro has not yet succeeded — individually restoring each remaining untested piece (a second IF node gating mascot logic, two Generate Image nodes, an unused Manual Trigger branch) does not reproduce it alone.

### Expected behavior

The Merge node should execute and pass data through once its immediate upstream (Route by Mascot) has reported success with the correct item split, matching the isolated repro (which merges successfully in <30ms with the identical IF → Execute Workflow → Merge node combination).

Ruled out:
- Merge waiting on a fully-skipped branch forever
- alwaysOutputData as workaround
- Random/transient failure (fully deterministic across 5 real runs + 1 clone)
- Task Runner acknowledgment timeout (a real "Runner took too long to acknowledge" log line was found, but the failure is ~200ms, far faster than the ~60s timeout window)
- Node-combination-specific bug (isolated verbatim repro works fine)
- Timing/ordering race (inserting a diagnostic NoOp node mid-edge didn't change the outcome)

Question: Is there a known execution-planning behavior tied to overall graph size/shape (e.g. diamond convergence patterns, or how expected-input counts are computed for Merge nodes) that could cause a Merge node to be silently marked as skipped in a large graph despite its immediate upstream reporting success?

items.body:
## Environment

- **n8n**: 2.31.0 (self-hosted, Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.31.0`, Alpine 3.24 base, Node.js v24.16.0 inside the container)
- **@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain**: 2.31.0 (bundled)
- **Nodes involved**: `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent` (typeVersion 1.7), `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChatAnthropic` (typeVersion 1.3)
- **Model**: `claude-sonnet-5` (Anthropic)
- **Tool node type used**: `n8n-nodes-base.postgresTool` (a regular node used as a tool via the "usable as tool" mechanism, not a purpose-built LangChain tool node)

## Symptom

With a real production workflow (Twilio WhatsApp assistant), the AI Agent never calls any of its connected tools when a large static `systemMessage` (~50KB, built from a business prompt template) is used. The model always finishes with `stop_reason: "end_turn"` (via the AI Agent's own text output — it never even attempts a tool call), narrating an intention to check something ("let me check...") and then answering from its own embedded knowledge/hallucination instead of calling any tool. No error is raised anywhere — the execution completes successfully.

This was fully reproducible and is **not intermittent** — confirmed across all real executions retained in the database (11 days of history).

## What this is NOT (ruled out with direct evidence)

- **Not the Anthropic API's payload validation / size limit.** The exact same request body (large `system`, `tools`, `messages`) that fails through the n8n AI Agent was sent **directly to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`** (bypassing n8n's LangChain node and our internal caching proxy entirely, using n8n's `httpRequest` node with `predefinedCredentialType`) and it worked correctly (`stop_reason: "tool_use"`), both as a plain string `system` and as the array-with-`cache_control` format our proxy produces.
- **Not a `$fromAI()` schema bug** (tracked separately, see below) — that bug (missing explicit type argument, matching #18588) was found and fixed independently; it does not explain this symptom on its own (see Cause #2).
- **Not our internal caching proxy** (source read in full — it does a JSON parse/mutate-`system`-only/stringify pass, no field is dropped; confirmed via direct byte-for-byte reproduction of its output sent straight to Anthropic).
- **Not the number of connected tools.** Full elimination matrix below.
- **Not prompt-caching related** (`cache_control` present or absent makes no difference at the API level, confirmed by direct testing both ways).

## Elimination matrix (prompt size × number of tools)

All runs below use the same isolated test workflow, same AI Agent/model config, same credential, only `systemMessage` length and the set of connected tools varied.

| systemMessage | # tools connected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| short (~100 bytes) | 1 | tool called |
| **long (~50KB)** | **1** | **tool NOT called** |
| long (~50KB) | 4 | tool NOT called |
| long (~50KB) | 7 (matches production) | tool NOT called |
| **short (~100 bytes)** | **7 (matches production)** | **tool called** |

Number of tools has **zero measurable effect** — only `systemMessage` length correlates with the failure.

## Two distinct, overlapping causes found under "large prompt"

### Cause #1 — tool node missing `toolDescription` (closed, root cause understood)

A `postgresTool` node with no `descriptionType`/`toolDescription` set at all (relying purely on default/auto behavior) fails to be included/used when `systemMessage` is large. The **same node, unmodified, with a short `systemMessage`, works fine** — so an empty description alone is not sufficient to reproduce it; it only manifests combined with a large prompt.

| systemMessage | tool has `toolDescription`? | Result |
|---|---|---|
| short | no | tool called |
| short | yes | tool called |
| long | **no** | **tool NOT called** |
| long | **yes** | **tool called** |

Direct-to-Anthropic confirmation: a tool schema with **no `description` field at all**, combined with the same ~50KB system prompt and cache_control, sent straight to the Anthropic API, still resulted in `stop_reason: "tool_use"` — the raw API tolerates a description-less tool fine, at any prompt size. So this is n8n-side behavior, not an Anthropic API constraint.

### Cause #2 — tool WITH a proper, well-formed `toolDescription` STILL fails with a large prompt (root cause NOT understood)

Using a *different* tool (`Consultar Preço do Serviço` in our production workflow) that has a clear, well-formed `toolDescription` string, connected **alone**, with the same ~50KB `systemMessage`: **the tool is still never called.** This rules out Cause #1 as the sole explanation — there is a second, distinct failure mode triggered by prompt size alone, independent of whether the tool has a description.

We have **not** identified the mechanism for Cause #2. It reproduces reliably in our environment but we stopped investigating further at this point to avoid speculation without evidence.

## Related but separate bug already fixed on our side (do not conflate)

Independently, we also found and fixed the known `$fromAI()` issue where omitting the explicit type argument (`$fromAI(key, description)` instead of `$fromAI(key, description, "string")`) can produce a malformed JSON Schema and cause a tool to be silently skipped — this matches #18588 and community reports of `"type": "None"` schemas. This is a **real, separate, already-understood bug** that we fixed by adding the explicit type to all our `$fromAI()` calls. It is not the cause of the symptom described in this issue — both Cause #1 and Cause #2 above were reproduced with the type argument already correctly present.

## How to reproduce (minimal workflows attached)

Two exportable minimal workflow JSON files are attached in a follow-up comment on this issue (reproduces with a placeholder Postgres/Anthropic credential swapped in):
- `repro_causa1_tool_sem_descricao.json` — single `postgresTool` with **no** `toolDescription`, large filler `systemMessage`. Fails to call the tool. Swap `AI Agent.parameters.options.systemMessage` to reference `{{ $json.systemPromptSmall }}` instead of `{{ $json.systemPrompt }}` to see it work.
- `repro_causa2_tool_com_descricao.json` — same setup, but the tool **has** a proper `toolDescription`. Still fails with the large prompt (Cause #2, mechanism unknown).

Both need an Anthropic credential and a Postgres credential (any reachable Postgres instance works — the query itself is trivial and only exists to give the tool a `$fromAI()` parameter). Replace the placeholder credential IDs before running.

To trigger: use "Execute workflow" from the n8n editor (Manual Trigger), send message "My name is Fernanda". Two complementary checks confirm whether the tool was genuinely invoked, and both were used throughout this investigation:

- **Per-node signal**: in the execution data, check whether the tool node's name appears as a key in `resultData.runData`, with a `metadata.subRun` entry and real extracted arguments under `data.ai_tool` — this confirms the model's tool-use loop actually reached that specific node. This is what the elimination matrix above is based on.
- **Full-payload signal**: n8n's execution record captures the exact request body sent to the model verbatim (under the chat model node's `inputOverride`). A full-text search for the literal substring `"tools"` across the complete execution JSON shows whether a `tools` array was present anywhere in that call. This is the method behind this report's central finding — 0 occurrences in every failing execution we inspected, versus present (and accepted) when the same payload was sent directly to `api.anthropic.com` bypassing n8n. Note `toolDescription` (the tool node's static config parameter) shows up regardless — that's workflow metadata, not the runtime request, and should not be confused with an actual `tools` array in the call.

Both checks agreed in every case we tested. The one thing that is **not** a valid signal is inferring tool use indirectly from a business-level side effect (e.g., "a database row was created, so the tool must have run") — in our production workflow a separate deterministic fallback (unrelated to the AI Agent's own tool-calling) can produce the same side effect from the model's plain text output, independent of whether any tool was actually invoked.

## Summary

- Confirmed: not an Anthropic API limitation (same payload works when sent directly).
- Confirmed: not proxy/cache-related, not tool-count related, not the `$fromAI()` type bug (fixed separately).
- Confirmed root cause for one specific pattern (Cause #1: missing `toolDescription` + large prompt).
- Confirmed real but unexplained second pattern (Cause #2: even a well-described tool fails under the same large-prompt condition) — reported as-is, without speculation on the internal mechanism, for maintainers to investigate further.

### Bug Description

`n8n import:credentials --separate` aborts with `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: NOT NULL constraint failed: credentials_entity.data` when the input directory also contains the workflow files that `n8n export:workflow --backup` writes - which is exactly the directory the CLI documentation's own examples produce. `import:workflow --separate` skips the credential file in the same directory; `import:credentials --separate` does not skip the workflow file, tries to insert it as a credential, and the whole import aborts, so the credentials that would have imported are not imported either.

Reproduced on 2.36.8 (2026-08-30) and again on 2.37.9 (2026-09-04), Docker image, SQLite.

### To Reproduce

The [CLI page](https://docs.n8n.io/deploy/host-n8n/configure-n8n/use-the-command-line) writes both exports into one directory:

```sh
n8n export:workflow    --backup --output=backups/latest/
n8n export:credentials --backup --output=backups/latest/
```

Then, on a fresh instance:

```sh
n8n import:workflow    --separate --input=backups/latest/   # ok
n8n import:credentials --separate --input=backups/latest/   # fails
```

Observed, on 2.37.9 with one workflow and one `httpHeaderAuth` credential exported:

```text
$ n8n import:workflow --separate --input=/home/node/restore/
Skipping invalid workflow file: /home/node/restore/xbNcOFBmxn4eb05i.json
Importing 1 workflows...
Successfully imported 1 workflow.

$ n8n import:credentials --separate --input=/home/node/restore/
An error occurred while importing credentials. See log messages for details.
SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: NOT NULL constraint failed: credentials_entity.data
(exit 1)
```

Control: the same `import:credentials` command against a directory holding only the credential file:

```text
Successfully imported 1 credential.
```

### Expected behavior

Either `import:credentials --separate` skips files that are not credentials, the way `import:workflow --separate` already skips files that are not workflows, or the documentation's examples write the two exports to different directories. I would be glad to send a PR for whichever you prefer.

### Debug Info

Collected from inside the container rather than from Help > About, since the reproduction is CLI-only:

```yaml
core:

  platform: docker (self-hosted)
  nodeJsVersion: 26.5.1
  database: sqlite
  executionMode: regular
storage:
  binary: memory
```

### Operating System

Docker, official image `n8nio/n8n:2.37.9` (Alpine), on a Docker Desktop host

### n8n Version

2.37.9 (also 2.36.8)

### Node.js Version

26.5.1 (the image's)

SQLite (default)

main (default)

self hosted

## Summary

`numberList()` with non-finite or fractional bounds throws a raw `RangeError: Invalid array length` instead of an `ExpressionExtensionError`. Inside an expression the raw error is swallowed and the expression silently evaluates to `undefined`/`null` — wrong data with no error trigger.

Real runs (`extendedFunctions.numberList`):

- `numberList(1, 5)` → length 5
- `numberList(NaN, 5)` → `RangeError: Invalid array length`
- `numberList(Infinity, 5)` → `RangeError: Invalid array length`
- `numberList(1.5, 5.7)` → `RangeError: Invalid array length` (size 5.2 is not a valid array length)

## Root cause

`size = Math.abs(start - end) + 1` flows unvalidated into `new Array(size)`. Sibling validators in the same expression family raise `ExpressionExtensionError` for bad input; this one lets the engine error escape.

## Expected

Non-finite or non-integer bounds raise a clear `ExpressionExtensionError` like every other input validation in the expression extensions.

items.body:
## Summary

`Array.chunk()` with a negative size never returns: the guard rejects only non-numbers and `0`, so `chunk(-1)` enters `for (i = 0; i < len; i += chunkSize)` with a negative step and loops forever. An expression like `={{ [1,2,3].chunk(-1) }}` hangs evaluation (denial of service via crafted workflow or corrupt data feeding the size argument).

Verified with real code (`packages/workflow/dist/cjs`):

- `chunk([1,2,3],[2])` → `[[1,2],[3]]`
- `chunk([1,2,3],[-1])` → never returns (killed after 6s, zero output)

## How to test

Evaluate `={{ [1,2,3].chunk(-1) }}` as a node parameter. Observe an `ExpressionExtensionError` now. Before the fix, evaluation hung forever.

## Root cause

The size validation in `chunk()` (`packages/workflow/src/extensions/array-extensions.ts`, mirrored in `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime`) only rejects non-numeric and zero sizes. Negative sizes (and `NaN`) slip through into the stepping loop.

## Expected

Non-positive sizes raise the same clear `ExpressionExtensionError` as other invalid arguments, instead of hanging.
items.title: Array.chunk() with negative size never returns (expression hang)

items.body:
## Summary

`String.urlDecode()` calls `decodeURI`/`decodeURIComponent` unwrapped, so malformed percent-encoding (for example stray `%` characters in real-world URLs) throws a raw `URIError`. Worse, inside an expression the error is swallowed and the expression silently evaluates to `undefined` — downstream nodes run on wrong data with no error trigger.

Verified per path (`packages/workflow`):

- direct call `urlDecode('%%%', [])` → throws `URIError: URI malformed`
- expression `={{ "%%%".urlDecode() }}` (legacy engine) → returns `undefined`, no error
- control `={{ "a%20b".urlDecode() }}` → `'a b'`

## How to test

Evaluate `={{ "%%%".urlDecode() }}` as a node parameter. Observe an `ExpressionExtensionError` now. Before the fix, it returned `undefined`.

## Root cause

Sibling converters in the same file (`parseJson`, `toInt`, `toDate`) wrap failures in `ExpressionExtensionError`, which the engines surface properly. `urlDecode` is the only one that lets the raw error escape.

## Expected

Malformed input raises a clear `ExpressionExtensionError` like every other string converter, instead of failing silently.
items.title: String.urlDecode() on malformed input fails silently instead of raising an error

items.body:
## Summary

On the legacy expression path, an expression that blows the stack (for example a very long `1+1+...` chain, correct answer 20001) silently evaluates to `null` instead of failing. The workflow then runs with wrong data and reports success.

Verified per engine (`packages/workflow`, `getParameterValue` on the same expression):

- legacy → returned `null` (wrong; correct value 20001)
- vm → throws `IsolateError`
- quickjs → throws `IsolateError`

## How to test

Set `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=legacy`. Evaluate `={{ 1+1+...+1 }}` (20000 additions) as a node parameter. Observe `null` instead of an error. Repeat with the vm engine and observe a proper error.

## Root cause

`renderExpression` in `packages/workflow/src/expression.ts` maps only `ExpressionError`, `SyntaxError`, and frontend `TypeError` to thrown errors. Any other error type from `evaluateExpression` — including `RangeError` from stack exhaustion — falls through to `return null`.

## Expected

Surface `RangeError` as a clear evaluation error on the legacy path, the same way the vm engines fail loudly. `null` must mean the expression evaluated to null, never that evaluation blew up.
items.title: Legacy expression path silently returns null on stack exhaustion instead of failing

items.body:
## Summary

A stored workflow with a huge connection `index` passes structural validation and then explodes memory on every open/run, because the destination-map fill loop has no cap. A few-byte payload turns into gigabytes:

- `index=100000` → 100001 buckets, +5MB heap, 10ms
- `index=500000` → 500001 buckets, +24MB heap, 42ms (linear; 50M ≈ 2.5GB)

## How to test

Save a workflow whose connections contain e.g. `{"A": {"main": [[{"node": "B", "type": "main", "index": 500000}]]}}`, then open or execute it. Watch heap grow linearly with the index. Any `new Workflow()` (constructor → `setConnections` → `mapConnectionsByDestination`) on such a stored workflow triggers it, so one saved payload breaks every open/run persistently.

## Root cause

- `packages/workflow/src/common/map-connections-by-destination.ts`: `for (let j = maxIndex; j < connectionInfo.index; j++) push([])` pads a dense array up to the raw index.
- `packages/workflow/src/workflow-structure-validation.ts`: the schema accepts `index: z.number().int().min(0)` with no upper bound, so the payload is considered structurally valid.

## Expected

Refuse absurd indexes fail-closed (throw on padding past a sane bound) so a stored payload errors loudly instead of OOMing the instance. Real node output indexes are single digits; nothing legitimate comes near the bound.

items.body:
### Bug Description

When the AI Agent (Tools Agent) V3 node has `retryOnFail: true` and hits its own `maxIterations` limit, the generic node-level retry mechanism retries the node's `execute()` without understanding the Agent's suspend/resume (`EngineRequest`/`EngineResponse`) protocol. This silently wipes all accumulated tool-call history and restarts the task from scratch, instead of surfacing a clean "max iterations reached" error. Critically, this can repeat indefinitely (not just once) - see mechanism below - resulting in unbounded, costly LLM/tool-call loops with no natural stopping point.

**Root cause (traced in source)**

- `checkMaxIterations()` (`packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/.../ToolsAgent/V3/helpers/checkMaxIterations.ts`) throws a `NodeOperationError` once `response.metadata.iterationCount >= maxIterations`.
- This is caught by the engine's generic retry loop in `packages/core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts`, which retries `runNode()` per `retryOnFail`/`maxTries`/`waitBetweenTries` - with no awareness of the Agent's own suspend/resume protocol.
- On retry, `toolsAgentExecute` is re-invoked and empirically receives no prior tool-call history, rather than continuing where it left off.
- The retry budget (`maxTries`) is scoped to a single "dequeue" of the node from the execution stack (one resume attempt), NOT the whole execution. Since a "successful" (even if context-reset) round returns a fresh `EngineRequest` and triggers `continue executionLoop` in the outer loop, the retry counter is effectively reset every `maxIterations` rounds. The reset-and-restart pattern is therefore NOT bounded by `maxTries` and can repeat for as many cycles as the task allows.

**Empirical evidence**

- The LLM prompt byte-length reverts to the exact baseline size (identical to the very first call) at every reset point - confirmed across 11 consecutive reset-cycles in one execution (105 total tool calls for a task that should have needed far fewer).
- A clean timing signature: the gap between a reset boundary's last tool-call completion and the next LLM call's start is consistently ~2000ms longer than normal round-to-round gaps (~500ms) - matching `waitBetweenTries: 2000` exactly, reproduced across multiple independent occurrences.
- Confirmed causally: disabling `retryOnFail` on the same node/task eliminates the reset entirely - the workflow now fails cleanly with "Max iterations (N) reached..." instead of resetting.

**Suggested fix**

`retryOnFail` should either not apply to a `NodeOperationError` thrown from `checkMaxIterations` (a deterministic, non-transient limit - not a transient failure retry could plausibly help with), or, when retrying an Agent V3 node mid-suspend/resume, the retry should preserve/reconstruct the full prior context before re-invoking `execute()`, so it genuinely continues instead of silently restarting.

**Current workaround**

Disable `retryOnFail` entirely on Agent V3 nodes. The node then fails cleanly (routable via `onError: continueErrorOutput`) instead of retrying - no functionality is lost, since retryOnFail's only observed effect here is the harmful reset behavior.

**Possibly related**

#22771 (Max Iterations routing to Success instead of Error output) and the sub-agent retry-configuration thread at https://community.n8n.io/t/ai-agent-with-sub-agent-tools-fails-workflow-stops-despite-retry-configuration/254011 both point at the same general area (Max Iterations / retryOnFail handling in Agent nodes) being under-tested, though neither documents this exact context-reset mechanism.

---

### To Reproduce

1. Create an AI Agent (Tools Agent) V3 node with a repeatable tool (e.g. a code-execution tool).
2. Leave `maxIterations` at default (10) or set it explicitly.
3. Enable Retry On Fail (maxTries >= 2) on the Agent node.
4. Give the agent a task requiring more rounds of tool calls than `maxIterations`.
5. Observe: instead of failing cleanly with "Max iterations (N) reached...", the agent's next LLM call is byte-identical to its very first call (no tool history) and it restarts the task from scratch - repeating this every `maxIterations` rounds, potentially indefinitely.

---

### Expected behavior

When `checkMaxIterations` throws because the iteration limit was reached, the node should either fail cleanly with the "Max iterations (N) reached..." error (as it does when `retryOnFail` is disabled), or - if retried - the retry should genuinely continue from the agent's actual prior state, not silently discard all accumulated tool-call history and restart the task from scratch.

---

<!-- Please follow the template below. Skip the questions that are not relevant to you. -->

## Describe the problem/error/question
Since 2026-09-03, a Respond to Webhook node no longer emits a Set-Cookie entry configured under Options → Response Headers. The header is dropped silently — no error, no warning, the execution is marked successful.

Other custom response headers from the same node are still emitted correctly. So this is specific to Set-Cookie; it is not "response headers stopped working", and it is not tied to one Respond With mode (Text and Redirect are both affected).

This broke our OIDC/SSO login completely, in two separate projects on the same instance, at the same moment. Nothing on our side changed: the two workflows involved were last modified 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-27.

We run an OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE flow entirely in n8n:

1. GET /webhook/sso-login responds with a 307 redirect to the IdP's /authorize, and sets a short-lived signed transaction cookie et_sso_tx (state, nonce, code_verifier, return_to; 10 minute expiry).
2. The IdP redirects the browser to GET /webhook/sso-callback.
3. The callback reads et_sso_tx from the request cookie header and verifies it with a JWT node.

Step 1 no longer sets the cookie, so step 3 gets an empty token and the workflow dies. The webhook then answers 200 with an empty body, which users see as a blank page after signing in.

Questions

1. Is this an intentional security change — e.g. to stop webhook responses from setting cookies on the n8n origin, where they could interfere with the editor's own auth cookies? If so, please document it in the release notes: it silently breaks any cookie-based flow built on webhooks.
2. If intentional — what is the recommended way to carry short-lived transaction state across an OIDC redirect now? We can move the signed state into the OAuth state parameter, but that removes the binding of the login transaction to the browser, which is exactly what the cookie provided (login-CSRF protection).
3. If it is a regression — is a fix planned, and is there a workaround in the meantime?

## What is the error message (if any)?
There is no error message for the dropped header itself — that is the core of the problem. The response is returned as configured, minus Set-Cookie, and the execution is marked successful.

The error we do see is the downstream consequence, in the JWT node that verifies the (now empty) cookie in the callback workflow:

ExpressionError: Invalid input for 'Token' [item 0]

## Please share your workflow/screenshots/recording
Minimal reproduction — a webhook that responds with two custom headers. Only one of them arrives.

{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "parameters": {
        "path": "set-cookie-probe",
        "responseMode": "responseNode",
        "options": {}
      },
      "type": "n8n-nodes-base.webhook",
      "typeVersion": 2.1,
      "position": [0, 0],
      "id": "3f0f1d2e-0a1b-4c2d-8e3f-4a5b6c7d8e9f",
      "name": "GET set-cookie-probe",
      "webhookId": "3f0f1d2e-0a1b-4c2d-8e3f-4a5b6c7d8e9f"
    },
    {
      "parameters": {
        "respondWith": "text",
        "responseBody": "probe",
        "options": {
          "responseHeaders": {
            "entries": [
              {
                "name": "X-Probe",
                "value": "wirkt"
              },
              {
                "name": "Set-Cookie",
                "value": "et_probe=1; Path=/webhook; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=60"
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      },
      "type": "n8n-nodes-base.respondToWebhook",
      "typeVersion": 1.5,
      "position": [220, 0],
      "id": "5b6c7d8e-9f0a-4b1c-8d2e-3f4a5b6c7d8e",
      "name": "Respond with two headers"
    }
  ],
  "connections": {
    "GET set-cookie-probe": {
      "main": [
        [
          {
            "node": "Respond with two headers",
            "type": "main",
            "index": 0
          }
        ]
      ]
    }
  },

}

## Share the output returned by the last node
The workflow runs successfully; the problem is only visible on the wire. Calling the production webhook:

$ curl -sD - -o /dev/null "https://<instance>.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/set-cookie-probe"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

x-probe arrives, which proves the node configuration is live and Response Headers are being applied. Set-Cookie is absent.

Expected output:

The same applies with Respond With: Redirect, which is how our SSO uses it — the 307 carries its Location header but no Set-Cookie:

Location: https://<idp>/connect/authorize?client_id=...
(no Set-Cookie header)

For contrast, non-cookie custom headers on other webhooks in the same instance are unaffected — Cache-Control: no-store and Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 still arrive as configured.

### Bug Description

ref: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/26544

Linting an n8n custom node project with ESLint 10 currently crashes because `@n8n/node-cli` depends on a version of `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` that is not compatible with ESLint 10.

ESLint 10 removed several deprecated rule context methods, including `context.getFilename()` and `context.getSourceCode()`.

While these APIs do not appear to be used directly by `@n8n/node-cli`, the currently used `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` 1.x does use them.

As a result, when ESLint 10 is used to lint an n8n custom node project, ESLint crashes with an error such as:

```text
Oops! Something went wrong! :(

ESLint: 10.9.1

TypeError: context.getFilename is not a function
```

This is particularly unexpected because `@n8n/node-cli` currently declares the following ESLint peer dependency:

```json
{
  "eslint": ">= 9"
}
```

which also allows ESLint 10.

`eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` has already addressed this incompatibility in:

https://github.com/ivov/eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base/pull/214

The fix replaces the removed context APIs with their property-based equivalents supported by ESLint 10.

The fix has been released as `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` 2.0.0.

I confirmed in my own project using `@n8n/node-cli` that the following overrides allow linting to work successfully with ESLint 10:

```yaml
overrides:
  "eslint": "10.9.1"
  "eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base": "2.0.0"
```

Therefore, I would like to propose updating `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` used by this repository to `2.0.0` (or `^2.0.0`) as a first step toward ESLint 10 compatibility.

Version 2.0.0 drops support for ESLint versions below 8.40. This should not affect the current n8n repository, as the repository currently uses ESLint 9.29.0.

This change would at least remove the current `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` blocker for using ESLint 10 in custom node projects.

### To Reproduce

1. Create or use an n8n custom node project using `@n8n/node-cli`.
2. Configure the project to use ESLint 10. For example:

```yaml
overrides:
  "eslint": "10.9.1"
```

3. Run the project's lint command.
4. ESLint crashes while executing a rule from `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` with an error such as:

```text
Oops! Something went wrong! :(

ESLint: 10.9.1

TypeError: context.getFilename is not a function
```

5. Add the following override:

```yaml
overrides:
  "eslint": "10.9.1"
  "eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base": "2.0.0"
```

6. Run lint again.
7. Linting now proceeds without the `context.getFilename` crash.

### Expected behavior

`@n8n/node-cli` should be able to lint custom node projects with versions of ESLint allowed by its declared peer dependency.

In particular, using ESLint 10 should not cause ESLint to crash because of deprecated rule context APIs in `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base`.

Updating `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` to version 2.0.0 should remove this incompatibility.

### Debug Info

Not applicable. This issue occurs in the ESLint tooling used for custom node development and does not require a running n8n instance.

macOS

2.37.7

### Node.js Version

24.19.0

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

## Describe the problem/error/question

Since the 2 September 2026 release (n8n 2.37.7 / 2.38.x, PR #37586 "chore: Bundle 2.x"), a Slack **HITL tool gate** (`n8n-nodes-base.slackHitlTool`, the "Human review" node attached to an AI Agent tool) with **Capture Responder** enabled can no longer be approved or declined. Every button click in Slack fails, the card is never updated, the gated tool never runs, and the execution stays in `waiting` until the Limit Wait Time expires.

Cause, from the shipped code: PR #37586 added a `platformNodeType` check to `packages/cli/src/webhooks/hitl-interaction-webhooks.ts`. `SlackInteractionWebhooks` sets `platformNodeType = 'n8n-nodes-base.slack'` and `validate()` now does:

```ts
if (node.type !== this.platformNodeType) return { ok: false, status: 404 };
```

The waiting node for a gate is `n8n-nodes-base.slackHitlTool`, not `n8n-nodes-base.slack`, so the interactivity callback is rejected with 404 before the resume. The PR adds a test that asserts 404 for any non-Slack node type, but the Slack HITL tool variant was not accounted for. The `getWebhookExecutionData()` path that runs afterwards already handles these nodes (`isHitlNode = node.type.endsWith('HitlTool')`), so only the new guard is wrong.

The same gate worked on the morning of 2 September (interactive Approve resumed the run, responder captured, card updated in place) and failed that evening with no workflow change. Plain `n8n-nodes-base.slack` Send and Wait nodes are unaffected. Setting `captureResponder: false` on the gate is a workaround (link buttons resume through `/webhook-waiting/<executionId>/<nodeId>`, which does handle HitlTool nodes), but you lose the responder identity and the post-decision card edit.

Suggested fix: accept the platform node type and its HITL tool variant, for example `node.type === this.platformNodeType || node.type === this.platformNodeType + 'HitlTool'`, or strip the `HitlTool` suffix before comparing. The sibling handlers for Telegram, Gmail, Teams and others presumably have the same problem.

Setup: n8n cloud (auto-upgraded 2 September 2026), Slack app with Interactivity enabled and Request URL set to `https://<instance>/webhook-waiting-slack`, Signature Secret set on the Slack credential, AI Agent v3 on Claude Sonnet 5, Slack node v2.5.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Import the workflow below, set a Slack bot credential and an Anthropic credential, publish.
2. In the chat, send "create a record called test".
3. The approval card appears in the Slack channel. Click Approve.

Expected: the run resumes, the gated tool executes, the card shows the outcome and who responded.

Actual: Slack shows a warning triangle with "This app responded with Status Code 404". Nothing happens in n8n. The execution stays in `waiting` and eventually times out.

## What is the error message (if any)?

No error in n8n. The execution stays in `waiting` and later resumes on the wait timeout with no decision. Slack shows a warning triangle on the button with the tooltip:

```
This app responded with Status Code 404
```
